```ts
// --- computePool -------------------------------------------------------------

export interface PoolDeps {
  contacts: Pick<ContactsRepo, 'getById' | 'listByType'>;
  units: Pick<UnitsRepo, 'getById' | 'listByStatus'>;
  placements: Pick<PlacementsRepo, 'hasActivePlacementForOtherTenant'>;
  orgNames: Pick<OrgNamesService, 'read'>;
  config: Pick<AppConfig, 'rankingPoolWindowDays' | 'rankingMaxPool' | 'rankingReadConcurrency'>;
  logger?: Logger;
}

export interface PoolOpts {
  /** Lifts the recency window (property anchor only; ignored for a tenant anchor). */
  includeOlder: boolean;
  now: Date;
}

interface PoolBase {
  ok: true;
  anchorNotes: AnchorNote[];
  /** Property anchor: its recorded authorities mapped. Tenant anchor: both empty. */
  authorities: AuthorityMapping;
  /** The organization list as read once for this pool; the cards map every property with it. */
  orgEntries: readonly OrgEntry[];
}

/** A property anchor: candidates are tenants, ascending contactId. */
export interface PropertyPool extends PoolBase {
  kind: 'unit';
  anchorRecord: UnitItem;
  candidates: ContactItem[];
}

/** A tenant anchor: candidates are properties, ascending unitId. */
export interface TenantPool extends PoolBase {
  kind: 'tenant';
  anchorRecord: ContactItem;
  candidates: UnitItem[];
}

export type PoolFailureReason = 'anchor_not_found' | 'org_list_failed' | 'pool_too_large';

export interface PoolFailure {
  ok: false;
  reason: PoolFailureReason;
  message: string;
  /**
   * pool_too_large only (PR16, FB4): the pool's size, the anchor (record,
   * and by kind), its notes and the organization list the pool read - what
   * the read's anchor block needs, its missing flags included
   * (assemble.ts poolTooLargeMissing). `anchorRecord` is `anchor.record`.
   */
  size?: number;
  anchorRecord?: ContactItem | UnitItem;
  anchor?: RankingAnchorRecord;
  anchorNotes?: AnchorNote[];
  orgEntries?: readonly OrgEntry[];
}

export type PoolResult = PropertyPool | TenantPool | PoolFailure;

export const POOL_MESSAGES = {
  anchorNotFound: 'This record was not found.',
  orgListFailed: 'The organization list could not be read, so the pool could not be worked out. Press Rank again.',
  poolTooLarge: (size: number): string => `Pool too large to rank (${size} candidates)`,
} as const;

const PAGE_SIZE = 200;

function compareIds(a: string, b: string): number {
  return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0;
}

function notFound(): PoolFailure {
  return { ok: false, reason: 'anchor_not_found', message: POOL_MESSAGES.anchorNotFound };
}

/** A rankable anchor's record, by kind. */
export type RankingAnchorRecord = { kind: 'unit'; record: UnitItem } | { kind: 'tenant'; record: ContactItem };

export interface AnchorReadDeps {
  contacts: Pick<ContactsRepo, 'getById'>;
  units: Pick<UnitsRepo, 'getById'>;
}

/**
 * PR21: THE anchor-exists rule (spec D12's 404), the ONE function the pool
 * and the rank claim (S5) use. A tenant anchor is a contact that exists, is
 * not soft-deleted and is typed `tenant`; a unit anchor is a unit that exists
 * and is not soft-deleted, ANY status. The anchor's state never refuses a
 * ranking (spec D1: anchor notes instead). Answers the record, or undefined.
 */
export async function readRankingAnchor(anchor: AnchorRef, deps: AnchorReadDeps): Promise<RankingAnchorRecord | undefined> {
  if (anchor.kind === 'tenant') {
    const contact = await deps.contacts.getById(anchor.id);
    if (contact === undefined || isContactDeleted(contact) || contact.type !== 'tenant') return undefined;
    return { kind: 'tenant', record: contact };
  }
  const unit = await deps.units.getById(anchor.id);
  if (unit === undefined || isUnitDeleted(unit)) return undefined;
  return { kind: 'unit', record: unit };
}

/** PR21: readRankingAnchor as a yes / no, for the rank claim (S5). */
export async function rankingAnchorExists(anchor: AnchorRef, deps: AnchorReadDeps): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await readRankingAnchor(anchor, deps)) !== undefined;
}

async function readOrgEntries(deps: PoolDeps): Promise<readonly OrgEntry[] | null> {
  try {
    return (await deps.orgNames.read()).entries;
  } catch (err) {
    deps.logger?.warn({ err }, 'ranking pool: the organization list read failed');
    return null;
  }
}

/** Every searching tenant, paged to the end (the read already hides soft-deleted contacts; the belts repeat it). */
async function listSearchingTenants(contacts: PoolDeps['contacts']): Promise<ContactItem[]> {
  const out: ContactItem[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  let exclusiveStartKey: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
  do {
    const page = await contacts.listByType('tenant', {
      status: 'searching',
      limit: PAGE_SIZE,
      ...(exclusiveStartKey !== undefined && { exclusiveStartKey }),
    });
    for (const contact of page.items) {
      if (contact.type !== 'tenant' || contact.status !== 'searching' || isContactDeleted(contact)) continue;
      if (seen.has(contact.contactId)) continue;
      seen.add(contact.contactId);
      out.push(contact);
    }
    exclusiveStartKey = page.lastEvaluatedKey;
  } while (exclusiveStartKey !== undefined);
  return out;
}

/** Every available unit, paged to the end (deleted excluded by the read; the belts repeat it). */
async function listAvailableUnits(units: PoolDeps['units']): Promise<UnitItem[]> {
  const out: UnitItem[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  let exclusiveStartKey: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
  do {
    const page = await units.listByStatus('available', {
      limit: PAGE_SIZE,
      ...(exclusiveStartKey !== undefined && { exclusiveStartKey }),
    });
    for (const unit of page.items) {
      if (unit.status !== 'available' || isUnitDeleted(unit)) continue;
      if (seen.has(unit.unitId)) continue;
      seen.add(unit.unitId);
      out.push(unit);
    }
    exclusiveStartKey = page.lastEvaluatedKey;
  } while (exclusiveStartKey !== undefined);
  return out;
}

function tooLarge(
  size: number,
  anchor: RankingAnchorRecord,
  anchorNotes: AnchorNote[],
  orgEntries: readonly OrgEntry[],
): PoolFailure {
  return {
    ok: false,
    reason: 'pool_too_large',
    size,
    message: POOL_MESSAGES.poolTooLarge(size),
    anchorRecord: anchor.record,
    anchor,
    anchorNotes,
    orgEntries,
  };
}

async function propertyPool(unit: UnitItem, opts: PoolOpts, deps: PoolDeps): Promise<PoolResult> {
  const orgEntries = await readOrgEntries(deps);
  if (orgEntries === null) return { ok: false, reason: 'org_list_failed', message: POOL_MESSAGES.orgListFailed };
  const authorities = mapAuthorities(orgEntries, authoritiesOf(unit));
  const sizes = unitVoucherSizes(unit);
  const windowDays = deps.config.rankingPoolWindowDays;
  const candidates = (await listSearchingTenants(deps.contacts))
    .filter(
      (contact) =>
        isSendable(contact) &&
        voucherSizeMatches(sizes, tenantVoucherSize(contact)) &&
        authorityAllows(authorities, contact['housingAuthority']) &&
        (opts.includeOlder || inPoolWindow(contact, opts.now, windowDays)),
    )
    .sort((a, b) => compareIds(a.contactId, b.contactId));
  const anchorNotes = unitAnchorNotes(unit);
  if (candidates.length > deps.config.rankingMaxPool) {
    return tooLarge(candidates.length, { kind: 'unit', record: unit }, anchorNotes, orgEntries);
  }
  return { ok: true, kind: 'unit', anchorRecord: unit, candidates, anchorNotes, authorities, orgEntries };
}

async function tenantPool(anchor: ContactItem, deps: PoolDeps): Promise<PoolResult> {
  const orgEntries = await readOrgEntries(deps);
  if (orgEntries === null) return { ok: false, reason: 'org_list_failed', message: POOL_MESSAGES.orgListFailed };
  const size = tenantVoucherSize(anchor);
  const fits = (await listAvailableUnits(deps.units)).filter(
    (unit) =>
      voucherSizeMatches(unitVoucherSizes(unit), size) &&
      authorityAllows(mapAuthorities(orgEntries, authoritiesOf(unit)), anchor['housingAuthority']),
  );
  // WI20: the question is "committed to a DIFFERENT tenant", so the anchor's own
  // placement on a unit never takes it out of the anchor's pool.
  const held = await mapWithConcurrency(fits, deps.config.rankingReadConcurrency, (unit) =>
    deps.placements.hasActivePlacementForOtherTenant(unit.unitId, anchor.contactId),
  );
  const candidates = fits.filter((_unit, index) => held[index] !== true).sort((a, b) => compareIds(a.unitId, b.unitId));
  const anchorNotes = tenantAnchorNotes(anchor);
  if (candidates.length > deps.config.rankingMaxPool) {
    return tooLarge(candidates.length, { kind: 'tenant', record: anchor }, anchorNotes, orgEntries);
  }
  return {
    ok: true,
    kind: 'tenant',
    anchorRecord: anchor,
    candidates,
    anchorNotes,
    authorities: { mapped: [], unmapped: [] },
    orgEntries,
  };
}

/**
 * Spec D1: the pool for `anchor` now. Fails (never throws for these) when the
 * anchor is not found (readRankingAnchor, PR21); when the organization list
 * cannot be read; or when the pool is above RANKING_MAX_POOL. Any other read
 * error propagates to the caller.
 */
export async function computePool(anchor: AnchorRef, opts: PoolOpts, deps: PoolDeps): Promise<PoolResult> {
  const found = await readRankingAnchor(anchor, deps);
  if (found === undefined) return notFound();
  return found.kind === 'unit' ? propertyPool(found.record, opts, deps) : tenantPool(found.record, deps);
}
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a (spec D2.1-D2.3; charter 6.1-6.2; plan PR3, PR7, WI12): THE two card
// builders. propertyCard and tenantCard are the ONLY functions that turn a
// record into what the model reads; the ranking job, the ranking read, the
// counterfactual check and every seen home call them (charter 6.2: one card
// per record, whichever side of the ranking it is on). Both are PURE;
// assemble.ts gathers their inputs.
//
// A card copies only the attributes cardFields.ts classifies `include` - an
// allowlist at runtime (charter 6.1) - in registry order, so the same record
// always serializes to the same bytes (spec D2.2). Free text is trimmed and
// otherwise passed as stored; an empty value is left off; nested objects are
// written with sorted keys (an address in its fixed part order). Requirement
// items are read through unitItemValue, so a legacy boolean `pets` reads as
// the No pets checkbox it means, for the card, the facts, completeness and
// the cap alike (spec D2.1).
import type { OrgEntry } from '../../lib/orgNames.js';
import { REQUIREMENT_ITEMS, isItemBlank, itemOfUnitKey, landlordItemValue, unitItemValue } from '../../lib/requirements.js';
import { authoritiesOf } from '../../lib/unitFields.js';
import type { ContactItem } from '../../repos/contactsRepo.js';
import type { UnitItem } from '../../repos/unitsRepo.js';
import {
  EXCLUDED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS,
  PROPERTY_CARD_FIELDS,
  PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS,
  RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS,
  includedFields,
  landlordTwin,
} from './cardFields.js';
import { mapAuthorities, recordedVoucherSizes, unitVoucherSizes } from './pool.js';
import type { Card } from './types.js';

export interface PropertyCardCtx {
  /** The organization list read once for this ranking (spec D1). */
  orgEntries: readonly OrgEntry[];
  /** RANKING_LANDLORD_CARD (spec D2.1). Off: nothing of the landlord's is read. */
  landlordCard: boolean;
  /** The landlord of record (`landlordId`), read only while the switch is on; null or absent = none on file. */
  landlord?: ContactItem | null;
}

/** What the cap (D9) and the unlawful-flag check (D10) read of a property's CURRENT card. */
export interface PropertyFacts {
  /** Requirement keys recorded on the card (a landlord default counts, switch on), registry order. */
  recordedRequirementKeys: string[];
  /** Each free-text field's trimmed text on the card; landlord defaults as `landlord:<key>`. */
  freeTextByField: Record<string, string>;
}

export const LANDLORD_DEFAULTS_KEY = 'landlordDefaults';

const REQUIREMENT_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS);
const FREE_TEXT_FIELDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS);
/** The requirement items a card may carry: every item but credit and income (A1). */
const RANKED_ITEMS = REQUIREMENT_ITEMS.filter((item) =>
  item.fields.every((field) => !EXCLUDED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS.includes(field.key)),
);
const ADDRESS_PARTS = ['line1', 'line2', 'city', 'state', 'zip'] as const;

/** Trimmed text, finite numbers, booleans, and arrays / objects of them; undefined = leave off. */
function cleanValue(raw: unknown): unknown {
  if (typeof raw === 'string') {
    const trimmed = raw.trim();
    return trimmed.length > 0 ? trimmed : undefined;
  }
  if (typeof raw === 'number') return Number.isFinite(raw) ? raw : undefined;
  if (typeof raw === 'boolean') return raw;
  if (Array.isArray(raw)) {
    const out = raw.map(cleanValue).filter((value) => value !== undefined);
    return out.length > 0 ? out : undefined;
  }
  if (raw !== null && typeof raw === 'object') {
    const source = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const key of Object.keys(source).sort()) {
      const value = cleanValue(source[key]);
      if (value !== undefined) out[key] = value;
    }
    return Object.keys(out).length > 0 ? out : undefined;
  }
  return undefined;
}

/** An address whole: the structured parts in their fixed order, or a legacy string as stored. */
function cleanAddress(raw: unknown): unknown {
  if (typeof raw === 'string') return cleanValue(raw);
  if (raw === null || typeof raw !== 'object' || Array.isArray(raw)) return undefined;
  const source = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const part of ADDRESS_PARTS) {
    const value = cleanValue(source[part]);
    if (typeof value === 'string') out[part] = value;
  }
  return Object.keys(out).length > 0 ? out : undefined;
}

/** `created_at` as a date (YYYY-MM-DD); any other text as stored. */
function dateOnly(raw: unknown): string | undefined {
  const value = cleanValue(raw);
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return undefined;
  return /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/.test(value) ? value.slice(0, 10) : value;
}

/** A stored attribute's card value. */
function storedValue(key: string, raw: unknown): unknown {
  if (key === 'address') return cleanAddress(raw);
  if (key === 'created_at') return dateOnly(raw);
  return cleanValue(raw);
}

/** A requirement key's value through unitItemValue; undefined when blank. */
function requirementValue(unit: UnitItem, key: string): string | number | true | undefined {
  const item = itemOfUnitKey(key);
  if (item === undefined) return undefined;
  const value = unitItemValue(unit, item.id)[key];
  return value === null || value === undefined ? undefined : value;
}

/**
 * Spec D2.1, switch on: the landlord of record's requirement values (through
 * landlordItemValue, credit and income left out) for every item the PROPERTY
 * records nothing for - the property's own value wins - plus the landlord
 * contact's notes. Undefined when the switch is off, there is no landlord, or
 * nothing is left.
 */
export function landlordDefaults(unit: UnitItem, ctx: PropertyCardCtx): Record<string, string | number | true> | undefined {
  const landlord = ctx.landlord;
  if (!ctx.landlordCard || landlord === undefined || landlord === null) return undefined;
  const out: Record<string, string | number | true> = {};
  for (const item of RANKED_ITEMS) {
    if (!isItemBlank(unitItemValue(unit, item.id))) continue;
    const value = landlordItemValue(landlord, item.id);
    for (const field of item.fields) {
      const fieldValue = value[field.key];
      if (fieldValue !== null && fieldValue !== undefined) out[field.key] = fieldValue;
    }
  }
  const notes = cleanValue(landlord['notes']);
  if (typeof notes === 'string') out['notes'] = notes;
  return Object.keys(out).length > 0 ? out : undefined;
}

/** Spec D2.1: the property card - included attributes, then voucher sizes, authorities and (switch on) the landlord defaults. */
export function propertyCard(unit: UnitItem, ctx: PropertyCardCtx): Card {
  const card: Card = {};
  for (const [key, field] of includedFields(PROPERTY_CARD_FIELDS)) {
    const value = REQUIREMENT_KEYS.has(key) ? requirementValue(unit, key) : storedValue(key, unit[key]);
    if (value !== undefined) card[field.cardKey ?? key] = value;
  }
  // FB20: the pool's one normalizer - whole sizes, clamped to 4 (4 means 4 or more).
  const sizes = unitVoucherSizes(unit);
  card['voucherSizes'] = sizes;
  card['voucherSizesInferredFromBeds'] = recordedVoucherSizes(unit).length === 0 && sizes.length > 0;
  card['authorities'] = mapAuthorities(ctx.orgEntries, authoritiesOf(unit));
  const defaults = landlordDefaults(unit, ctx);
  if (defaults !== undefined) card[LANDLORD_DEFAULTS_KEY] = defaults;
  return card;
}

/** Spec D2.1, D5, D9, D10: the recorded requirement keys and the free-text fields of the CURRENT card. */
export function propertyFacts(unit: UnitItem, ctx: PropertyCardCtx): PropertyFacts {
  const defaults = landlordDefaults(unit, ctx) ?? {};
  const recordedRequirementKeys = RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS.filter(
    (key) => requirementValue(unit, key) !== undefined || defaults[key] !== undefined,
  );
  const freeTextByField: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const field of PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS) {
    const value = REQUIREMENT_KEYS.has(field) ? requirementValue(unit, field) : cleanValue(unit[field]);
    if (typeof value === 'string') freeTextByField[field] = value;
  }
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(defaults)) {
    if (typeof value === 'string' && FREE_TEXT_FIELDS.has(key)) freeTextByField[landlordTwin(key)] = value;
  }
  return { recordedRequirementKeys, freeTextByField };
}
```

```ts
// --- The tenant card (spec D2.1-D2.3) ----------------------------------------

export interface TenantCardCtx {
  now: Date;
  /** RANKING_SEEN_MAX: how many properties-seen entries the card lists, in all. */
  seenMax: number;
  /** The UNBOUNDED seen set (seenSet.ts buildSeenSet). */
  seen: readonly SeenHome[];
}

/** One listed properties-seen entry (spec D2.3). */
export interface PropertiesSeenEntry {
  /** The home's unitId - a REFERENCE the prompt replaces with the home's handle; never sent as is. */
  home: string;
  label: string;
  sends: SendFact[];
  daysSinceLastSend: number | null;
  declined: { by: string; at: string } | null;
  tours: TourProjection[];
  /** The Notes lines that name this home. */
  feedback: string[];
}

export type RecencyBucket = 'this week' | 'this month' | 'one to three months' | 'older' | 'never';

export const TENANT_NOTES_KEY = 'notes';
export const LAST_HEARD_FROM_KEY = 'lastHeardFrom';
export const PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY = 'propertiesSeen';

/** Charter 9.1: this week (under 7 days), this month (under 30), one to three months (under 90), older, never. */
export function recencyBucket(lastHeardFromAt: unknown, now: Date): RecencyBucket {
  const at = instantMs(lastHeardFromAt);
  if (at === undefined) return 'never';
  const days = (now.getTime() - at) / DAY_MS;
  if (days < 7) return 'this week';
  if (days < 30) return 'this month';
  if (days < 90) return 'one to three months';
  return 'older';
}

function compareText(a: string, b: string): number {
  return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0;
}

/** Newest first; an entry with no instant last. */
function compareNewestFirst(a: string | null, b: string | null): number {
  const left = instantMs(a);
  const right = instantMs(b);
  if (left === undefined && right === undefined) return 0;
  if (left === undefined) return 1;
  if (right === undefined) return -1;
  return right - left;
}

interface ArrangedSeen {
  notes: string | undefined;
  entries: PropertiesSeenEntry[];
}

/**
 * Spec D2.3: the attach step over the whole seen set, then the bound. Entries
 * carrying an outcome (a decline, a tour, a feedback line) come first, newest
 * activity first; bare sends fill the remaining slots, newest send first. A
 * line naming a LISTED entry leaves the notes; a line naming only unlisted
 * entries stays, so no feedback is lost to the bound.
 */
function arrangePropertiesSeen(notes: unknown, ctx: TenantCardCtx): ArrangedSeen {
  const lines = attachFeedback(
    notes,
    ctx.seen.map((home) => ({ unitId: home.unitId, label: home.attachLabel })),
  );
  const feedbackByUnit = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const line of lines) {
    for (const unitId of line.unitIds) {
      const list = feedbackByUnit.get(unitId) ?? [];
      list.push(line.text);
      feedbackByUnit.set(unitId, list);
    }
  }
  const rows = ctx.seen.map((home) => ({ home, feedback: feedbackByUnit.get(home.unitId) ?? [] }));
  const hasOutcome = (row: { home: SeenHome; feedback: string[] }): boolean =>
    row.home.declined !== null || row.home.tours.length > 0 || row.feedback.length > 0;
  const withOutcome = rows
    .filter(hasOutcome)
    .sort((a, b) => compareNewestFirst(a.home.activityAt, b.home.activityAt) || compareText(a.home.unitId, b.home.unitId));
  const bare = rows
    .filter((row) => !hasOutcome(row))
    .sort((a, b) => compareNewestFirst(a.home.lastSendAt, b.home.lastSendAt) || compareText(a.home.unitId, b.home.unitId));
  const listed = [...withOutcome, ...bare].slice(0, Math.max(0, Math.floor(ctx.seenMax)));
  const listedIds = new Set(listed.map((row) => row.home.unitId));
  const moved = lines.some((line) => line.unitIds.some((unitId) => listedIds.has(unitId)));
  const general = lines.filter((line) => !line.unitIds.some((unitId) => listedIds.has(unitId))).map((line) => line.text);
  // FB21: when no line moves, the Notes text stays as stored (trimmed), its
  // line breaks and blank lines kept; only a box that lost lines is rebuilt.
  const stored = typeof notes === 'string' ? notes.trim() : '';
  return {
    notes: moved ? (general.length > 0 ? general.join('\n') : undefined) : stored.length > 0 ? stored : undefined,
    entries: listed.map(({ home, feedback }) => ({
      home: home.unitId,
      label: home.label,
      sends: home.sends.map((send) => ({ ...send })),
      daysSinceLastSend: daysSince(home.lastSendAt, ctx.now),
      declined: home.declined === null ? null : { ...home.declined },
      tours: home.tours.map((tour) => ({ ...tour })),
      feedback: [...feedback],
    })),
  };
}

/** Spec D2.1-D2.3: the tenant card - included attributes, the matching inputs by label, the recency bucket, properties seen. */
export function tenantCard(contact: ContactItem, ctx: TenantCardCtx): Card {
  const arranged = arrangePropertiesSeen(contact[TENANT_NOTES_KEY], ctx);
  const card: Card = {};
  for (const [key, field] of includedFields(TENANT_CARD_FIELDS)) {
    const value = key === TENANT_NOTES_KEY ? arranged.notes : storedValue(key, contact[key]);
    if (value !== undefined) card[field.cardKey ?? key] = value;
  }
  card[LAST_HEARD_FROM_KEY] = recencyBucket(contact.last_heard_from_at, ctx.now);
  card[PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY] = arranged.entries;
  return card;
}

/** The unitIds of a tenant card's listed properties-seen entries, in card order. */
export function listedHomeIds(card: Card): string[] {
  const listed = card[PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY];
  if (!Array.isArray(listed)) return [];
  return listed.flatMap((entry: unknown) =>
    entry !== null && typeof entry === 'object' && typeof (entry as PropertiesSeenEntry).home === 'string'
      ? [(entry as PropertiesSeenEntry).home]
      : [],
  );
}
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a (spec D3; charter 7.3; plan PR6): the completeness pass. Code marks
// each card's gaps against a FIXED list, each a stable key with a staff label;
// the flags go to the model with the card (`missing: [labels]`) and come back
// on the match as missing[] (mergeMissing). Missing data never stops a
// ranking. The tenant's matching inputs are marked by the ONE list
// (TENANT_MATCHING_INPUTS, its `completeness` flag) - this file never spells
// their keys.
import { isItemBlank, unitItemValue } from '../../lib/requirements.js';
import { TENANT_MATCHING_INPUTS, type TenantMatchingInput } from '../../lib/tenantMatchingInputs.js';
import { authoritiesOf } from '../../lib/unitFields.js';
import type { ContactItem } from '../../repos/contactsRepo.js';
import type { UnitItem } from '../../repos/unitsRepo.js';
import { landlordDefaults, type PropertyCardCtx } from './cards.js';
import { mapAuthorities, recordedVoucherSizes } from './pool.js';
import type { MissingFlag } from './types.js';

export const PROPERTY_MISSING_LABELS = {
  rent: 'Rent',
  payment_standard: 'Payment standard',
  voucher_sizes: 'Voucher sizes',
  authorities_unmapped: 'Housing authority not on the organization list',
  pets: 'Pets',
  accessibility: 'Accessibility',
} as const;

export const TENANT_MISSING_LABELS = {
  voucher_size: 'Voucher size',
  housing_authority: 'Housing authority',
} as const;

/** One item of a match's missing[] (spec D8): a code flag carries its key, a model unknown does not. */
export interface MissingEntry {
  key?: string;
  text: string;
}

const PETS_KEYS = ['no_pets', 'pets', 'pet_fee'] as const;

function isNumber(value: unknown): boolean {
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value);
}

function hasText(value: unknown): boolean {
  return typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0;
}

/** Spec D3, property: rent, payment standard, recorded voucher sizes, unmapped authorities, pets, accessibility. */
export function propertyMissing(unit: UnitItem, ctx: PropertyCardCtx): MissingFlag[] {
  const flags: MissingFlag[] = [];
  const add = (key: keyof typeof PROPERTY_MISSING_LABELS): void => {
    flags.push({ key, label: PROPERTY_MISSING_LABELS[key] });
  };
  if (!isNumber(unit.rent_min) && !isNumber(unit.rent_max) && !isNumber(unit.final_rent)) add('rent');
  if (!isNumber(unit.payment_standard)) add('payment_standard');
  // Only a RECORDED size counts (a size inferred from beds is missing), read
  // through the pool's one normalizer: a stored 2.5 is no size (FB20).
  if (recordedVoucherSizes(unit).length === 0) add('voucher_sizes');
  if (mapAuthorities(ctx.orgEntries, authoritiesOf(unit)).unmapped.length > 0) add('authorities_unmapped');
  const defaults = landlordDefaults(unit, ctx) ?? {};
  const petsByDefault = PETS_KEYS.some((key) => defaults[key] !== undefined);
  if (isItemBlank(unitItemValue(unit, 'pets')) && !petsByDefault) add('pets');
  if (!hasText(unit.accessibility)) add('accessibility');
  return flags;
}

/** The list fields tenantMissing reads (a test passes its own list). */
export type CompletenessInput = Pick<TenantMatchingInput, 'key' | 'label' | 'kind' | 'source' | 'completeness'>;

/**
 * Spec D3, tenant: voucher size, housing authority, and every list input
 * marked for completeness WHOSE SOURCE IS `field` (R2F10) - the same inputs
 * the card carries (cardFields.ts matchingInputCardFields); an input kept in
 * Notes is judged by the model from the Notes box, never from a stale
 * attribute.
 */
export function tenantMissing(
  contact: ContactItem,
  inputs: readonly CompletenessInput[] = TENANT_MATCHING_INPUTS,
): MissingFlag[] {
  const flags: MissingFlag[] = [];
  const size = contact['voucherSize'];
  if (!(typeof size === 'number' && Number.isInteger(size))) {
    flags.push({ key: 'voucher_size', label: TENANT_MISSING_LABELS.voucher_size });
  }
  if (!hasText(contact['housingAuthority'])) {
    flags.push({ key: 'housing_authority', label: TENANT_MISSING_LABELS.housing_authority });
  }
  for (const input of inputs) {
    if (!input.completeness || input.source !== 'field') continue;
    const value = contact[input.key];
    const present = input.kind === 'dollars' ? isNumber(value) : hasText(value);
    if (!present) flags.push({ key: input.key, label: input.label });
  }
  return flags;
}

function fold(text: string): string {
  return text.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
}

/** Spec D3: the code flags first (with their keys), then each model unknown not equal to one, once. */
export function mergeMissing(flags: readonly MissingFlag[], unknowns: readonly string[]): MissingEntry[] {
  const out: MissingEntry[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const flag of flags) {
    const folded = fold(flag.label);
    if (seen.has(folded)) continue;
    seen.add(folded);
    out.push({ key: flag.key, text: flag.label });
  }
  for (const raw of unknowns) {
    if (typeof raw !== 'string') continue;
    const text = raw.trim();
    const folded = fold(text);
    if (folded === '' || seen.has(folded)) continue;
    seen.add(folded);
    out.push({ text });
  }
  return out;
}
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a (spec D13; charter 10.3): the three fingerprints a match stores -
// sha256 over a STABLE serialization (object keys sorted at every depth,
// array order kept, undefined dropped).
//
// - unitCard: the property card as sent (landlord defaults included when the
//   switch is on).
// - pairHistory: the declined record and the tours (the tour projection);
//   never the send dates (age covers time since the last send).
// - tenantCard: NOT the card as arranged for the prompt (the arrangement
//   moves with sends: their order and the bound). It covers the card's own
//   fields WITHOUT `notes` and `propertiesSeen`; the Notes box text AS STORED
//   (every feedback line is a Notes line, so a new line or a staff edit
//   changes it wherever it would be arranged); and, for every property in the
//   UNBOUNDED seen set with a STORED outcome (a decline or a tour), sorted by
//   unitId, { unitId, label, unitCard, declined, tours }. So a bare send, a
//   re-send, an eviction from the listed entries and a line re-attaching
//   under a newly sent home change nothing; a decline, a tour or a feedback
//   line about ANY property, or an edit to any card field of a home with a
//   decline or a tour, changes every match of that tenant. Recency enters only
//   as its bucket (the card's lastHeardFrom).
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY, TENANT_NOTES_KEY } from './cards.js';
import type { SeenHome } from './seenSet.js';
import type { Card, PairHistory } from './types.js';

/** JSON with object keys sorted at every depth; undefined values dropped (null in an array). */
export function stableStringify(value: unknown): string {
  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') return JSON.stringify(value) ?? 'null';
  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    return `[${value.map((item) => (item === undefined ? 'null' : stableStringify(item))).join(',')}]`;
  }
  const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const keys = Object.keys(record)
    .filter((key) => record[key] !== undefined)
    .sort();
  return `{${keys.map((key) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${stableStringify(record[key])}`).join(',')}}`;
}

export function sha256Hex(text: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('hex');
}

/** Spec D13: the property card as sent. */
export function unitCardFingerprint(card: Card): string {
  return sha256Hex(stableStringify(card));
}

/** Spec D13: the declined record and the tours, never the sends. */
export function pairHistoryFingerprint(history: Pick<PairHistory, 'declined' | 'tours'>): string {
  return sha256Hex(stableStringify({ declined: history.declined, tours: history.tours }));
}

export interface TenantFingerprintInput {
  /** The tenant card (tenantCard). */
  card: Card;
  /** The contact's stored Notes box. */
  notesText: unknown;
  /** The UNBOUNDED seen set. */
  seen: readonly SeenHome[];
  /** A seen home's card fingerprint (null: a home a complete read did not find). Asked only for outcome homes. */
  homeCardFingerprint: (unitId: string) => string | null;
}

/** Spec D13: the tenant card fingerprint. */
export function tenantCardFingerprint(input: TenantFingerprintInput): string {
  const fields: Card = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(input.card)) {
    if (key === TENANT_NOTES_KEY || key === PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY) continue;
    fields[key] = value;
  }
  const seenOutcomes = input.seen
    .filter((home) => home.declined !== null || home.tours.length > 0)
    .sort((a, b) => (a.unitId < b.unitId ? -1 : a.unitId > b.unitId ? 1 : 0))
    .map((home) => ({
      unitId: home.unitId,
      label: home.label,
      unitCard: input.homeCardFingerprint(home.unitId),
      declined: home.declined,
      tours: home.tours,
    }));
  return sha256Hex(
    stableStringify({
      fields,
      notes: typeof input.notesText === 'string' ? input.notesText : '',
      seenOutcomes,
    }),
  );
}
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a (spec D1, D2, D3, D13; plan PR3, WI11, WI12): THE ONE GATHERER the
// ranking job (S5) and the ranking read (S6) share, so both always score and
// judge from the same pool, the same cards and the same fingerprints.
//
// The two SIDES are pure and exported, so the counterfactual check (S8) builds
// its synthetic cards through exactly this code:
// - buildTenantSide: the unbounded seen set, the tenant card (tenantCard), its
//   gaps, the full card (propertyCard) of each LISTED seen home and the
//   tenant fingerprint over every seen home with a stored outcome.
// - buildPropertySide: the property card, its gaps, its facts (for the cap
//   and the flag check) and its fingerprint.
import type { OrgEntry } from '../../lib/orgNames.js';
import type { ContactItem } from '../../repos/contactsRepo.js';
import type { ListingSendItem } from '../../repos/listingSendsRepo.js';
import type { TourItem } from '../../repos/toursRepo.js';
import type { UnitItem } from '../../repos/unitsRepo.js';
import { listedHomeIds, propertyCard, propertyFacts, tenantCard, type PropertyCardCtx, type PropertyFacts } from './cards.js';
import { propertyMissing, tenantMissing } from './completeness.js';
import { tenantCardFingerprint, unitCardFingerprint } from './fingerprints.js';
import { MISSING_UNIT_LABEL, buildSeenSet, type SeenHome } from './seenSet.js';
import type { Card, MissingFlag } from './types.js';

/** One tenant's card inputs: its listed sends, its tours, the seen units (one complete read) and, switch on, their landlords. */
export interface TenantReads {
  sends: ListingSendItem[];
  tours: TourItem[];
  units: ReadonlyMap<string, UnitItem>;
  landlords: ReadonlyMap<string, ContactItem>;
}

export interface SideCtx {
  now: Date;
  /** RANKING_SEEN_MAX. */
  seenMax: number;
  orgEntries: readonly OrgEntry[];
  /** RANKING_LANDLORD_CARD. */
  landlordCard: boolean;
}

/** A listed seen home as the call writes it once (spec D4): its label and its FULL property card. */
export interface SeenHomeCard {
  label: string;
  card: Card;
}

export interface TenantSide {
  card: Card;
  missing: MissingFlag[];
  /** The unbounded seen set. */
  seen: SeenHome[];
  /** The LISTED seen homes only, in card order. A home a complete read did not find has an empty card. */
  homes: Map<string, SeenHomeCard>;
  fingerprint: string;
}

export interface PropertySide {
  card: Card;
  missing: MissingFlag[];
  facts: PropertyFacts;
  fingerprint: string;
}

/** The property side: card, gaps, facts and fingerprint (spec D2.1, D3, D13). */
export function buildPropertySide(unit: UnitItem, ctx: PropertyCardCtx): PropertySide {
  const card = propertyCard(unit, ctx);
  return { card, missing: propertyMissing(unit, ctx), facts: propertyFacts(unit, ctx), fingerprint: unitCardFingerprint(card) };
}

function landlordOf(unit: UnitItem, landlords: ReadonlyMap<string, ContactItem>): ContactItem | null {
  return typeof unit.landlordId === 'string' && unit.landlordId.length > 0 ? (landlords.get(unit.landlordId) ?? null) : null;
}

/** The tenant side (spec D2.1-D2.3, D3, D13). Pure. */
export function buildTenantSide(contact: ContactItem, reads: TenantReads, ctx: SideCtx): TenantSide {
  const seen = buildSeenSet(reads);
  const homeCards = new Map<string, Card>();
  for (const home of seen) {
    if (home.unit === null) continue;
    homeCards.set(
      home.unitId,
      propertyCard(home.unit, {
        orgEntries: ctx.orgEntries,
        landlordCard: ctx.landlordCard,
        landlord: landlordOf(home.unit, reads.landlords),
      }),
    );
  }
  const card = tenantCard(contact, { now: ctx.now, seenMax: ctx.seenMax, seen });
  const fingerprint = tenantCardFingerprint({
    card,
    notesText: contact['notes'],
    seen,
    homeCardFingerprint: (unitId) => {
      const homeCard = homeCards.get(unitId);
      return homeCard === undefined ? null : unitCardFingerprint(homeCard);
    },
  });
  const labels = new Map(seen.map((home) => [home.unitId, home.label] as const));
  const homes = new Map<string, SeenHomeCard>();
  for (const unitId of listedHomeIds(card)) {
    homes.set(unitId, { label: labels.get(unitId) ?? MISSING_UNIT_LABEL, card: homeCards.get(unitId) ?? {} });
  }
  return { card, missing: tenantMissing(contact), seen, homes, fingerprint };
}
```

```ts
    expect(result.candidates.map((c) => [c.candidateId, c.tenantId, c.unitId, c.unverified, c.display, c.hasConsent])).toEqual([
      ['t1', 't1', 'u1', false, 'Pat t1', true],
      ['t2', 't2', 'u1', false, 'Pat t2', false],
      ['t3', 't3', 'u1', false, 'Pat t3', true],
    ]);
    const t1Side = buildTenantSide(
      T1,
      { sends: [S_T1_U1, S_T1_U2], tours: [], units: new Map([['u1', U1], ['u2', U2]]), landlords: new Map() },
      SIDE_CTX,
    );
    const c1 = verified(result.candidates[0]);
    expect(c1.card).toEqual(t1Side.card);
    expect(c1.missing).toEqual(t1Side.missing);
    expect(c1.pairHistory).toEqual({
      sends: [{ at: daysAgo(8), kind: 'sent' }],
      declined: { by: 'staff', at: daysAgo(5) },
      tours: [],
      daysSinceLastSend: 8,
    });
    expect(c1.fingerprints).toEqual({
      tenantCard: t1Side.fingerprint,
      unitCard: anchorSide.fingerprint,
      pairHistory: pairHistoryFingerprint(c1.pairHistory),
    });
    expect(c1.propertyFacts).toEqual(anchorSide.facts);
    expect(verified(result.candidates[2]).pairHistory).toEqual({ sends: [], declined: null, tours: [], daysSinceLastSend: null });
    expect([...result.homes.keys()]).toEqual(['u1', 'u2', 'u3']);
    expect(result.homes.get('u3')).toEqual({ label: 'u3 Main St, Decatur', card: propertyCard(U3, OFF) });
    expect(result.unverifiedCount).toBe(0);
  });

  it('reads each tenant card with one sends read and ONE units batch read for its whole seen set', async () => {
    const w = world();
    await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps);
    expect([...w.calls.listByContact].sort()).toEqual(['t1', 't2', 't3']);
    expect(w.calls.unitBatchReads.map((ids) => ids.join(',')).sort()).toEqual(['u1,u2', 'u3']);
  });

  it('an incomplete units read leaves only that candidate unverified, never "not on file"', async () => {
    const w = world();
    w.state.incompleteIds.add('u3');
    const result = ok(await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps));
    expect(result.candidates[1]).toEqual({
      tenantId: 't2',
      unitId: 'u1',
      candidateId: 't2',
      display: 'Pat t2',
      record: T2,
      hasConsent: false,
      unverified: true,
      card: null,
      missing: null,
      pairHistory: null,
      fingerprints: null,
      propertyFacts: buildPropertySide(U1, OFF).facts,
    });
    expect(result.candidates.map((c) => c.unverified)).toEqual([false, true, false]);
    expect([...result.homes.keys()]).toEqual(['u1', 'u2']);
    expect(result.unverifiedCount).toBe(1);
  });

  it('PR17: a failed tours read leaves that candidate unverified; assembleRanking never throws for a candidate', async () => {
    const w = world();
    w.state.failingTourReads.add('t1');
    const result = ok(await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps));
    expect(result.candidates.map((c) => [c.candidateId, c.unverified])).toEqual([
      ['t1', true],
      ['t2', false],
      ['t3', false],
    ]);
    expect([...result.homes.keys()]).toEqual(['u3']);
  });

  it('IR7: the display is always a string - a name else the contactId, a label else the no-address placeholder', async () => {
    const legacy = { ...unit('u-legacy'), address: '9 Old Rd, Atlanta, GA 30310' } as unknown as UnitItem;
    const noName = tenant('t-noname', { firstName: undefined, lastName: undefined });
    const w = world({ units: [U1, U2, U3, legacy], contacts: [noName] });
    const result = ok(await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u-legacy' }, OPTS, w.deps));
    expect(result.anchor.display).toBe(NO_ADDRESS_LABEL);
    expect(result.candidates.find((c) => c.candidateId === 't-noname')?.display).toBe('t-noname');
    expect(tenantDisplay(T1)).toBe('Pat t1');
    expect(propertyDisplay(U1)).toBe('u1 Main St, Decatur');
  });

  it('a failed sends read leaves that candidate unverified too', async () => {
    const w = world();
    w.state.failingSendReads.add('t3');
    const result = ok(await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps));
    expect(result.candidates.map((c) => [c.candidateId, c.unverified])).toEqual([
      ['t1', false],
      ['t2', false],
      ['t3', true],
    ]);
    expect(result.unverifiedCount).toBe(1);
  });

  it('runs at most RANKING_READ_CONCURRENCY candidate reads at once', async () => {
    const many = ['t4', 't5', 't6'].map((id) => tenant(id));
    const w = world({ contacts: many, config: { rankingReadConcurrency: 2 } });
    w.state.sendReadDelayMs = 5;
    await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps);
    expect(w.calls.listByContact).toHaveLength(6);
    expect(w.calls.maxInFlightSendReads).toBe(2);
  });

  it('a pool failure passes through and no card is read', async () => {
    const failing = world();
    failing.state.orgListFails = true;
    expect(await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, failing.deps)).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      reason: 'org_list_failed',
      message: POOL_MESSAGES.orgListFailed,
    });
    expect(failing.calls.listByContact).toEqual([]);
    const tooMany = world({ config: { rankingMaxPool: 1 } });
    expect(await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, tooMany.deps)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, reason: 'pool_too_large', size: 3 });
    expect(tooMany.calls.listByContact).toEqual([]);
    expect(await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u-nope' }, OPTS, world().deps)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, reason: 'anchor_not_found' });
  });
});

describe('tenant anchor - the properties of one tenant', () => {

describe('poolTooLargeMissing - the anchor gaps over the ceiling (FB4, PR16)', () => {
  it('a property anchor: propertyMissing with the pool organization list; a tenant anchor: tenantMissing', async () => {
    const w = world({ config: { rankingMaxPool: 1 } });
    const overUnit = await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps);
    if (overUnit.ok || overUnit.reason !== 'pool_too_large') throw new Error('expected pool_too_large');
    expect(await poolTooLargeMissing(overUnit, w.deps)).toEqual(propertyMissing(U1, OFF));
    const overTenant = await assembleRanking({ kind: 'tenant', id: 't1' }, OPTS, w.deps);
    if (overTenant.ok || overTenant.reason !== 'pool_too_large') throw new Error('expected pool_too_large');
    expect(await poolTooLargeMissing(overTenant, w.deps)).toEqual(tenantMissing(T1));
  });

  it("switch on: reads the property anchor's landlord; a landlord read that cannot finish throws", async () => {
    const w = world({ config: { rankingMaxPool: 1, rankingLandlordCard: true } });
    const over = await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps);
    if (over.ok || over.reason !== 'pool_too_large') throw new Error('expected pool_too_large');
    expect(await poolTooLargeMissing(over, w.deps)).toEqual(
      propertyMissing(U1, { orgEntries: ORG_ENTRIES, landlordCard: true, landlord: LANDLORD_1 }),
    );
    w.state.incompleteIds.add('contact-landlord-1');
    await expect(poolTooLargeMissing(over, w.deps)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(IncompleteBatchReadError);
  });

  it('any other failure carries no anchor gaps', async () => {
    const w = world();
    w.state.orgListFails = true;
    const failed = await assembleRanking({ kind: 'unit', id: 'u1' }, OPTS, w.deps);
    if (failed.ok || failed.reason !== 'org_list_failed') throw new Error('expected org_list_failed');
    expect(await poolTooLargeMissing(failed, w.deps)).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

```ts
// --- assembleRanking -----------------------------------------------------------

export interface AssembleDeps extends PoolDeps {
  contacts: Pick<ContactsRepo, 'getById' | 'listByType' | 'getManyByIds'>;
  units: Pick<UnitsRepo, 'getById' | 'listByStatus' | 'getManyByIds'>;
  listingSends: Pick<ListingSendsRepo, 'listByContact'>;
  tours: Pick<ToursRepo, 'listByTenant'>;
  config: Pick<
    AppConfig,
    'rankingPoolWindowDays' | 'rankingMaxPool' | 'rankingReadConcurrency' | 'rankingSeenMax' | 'rankingLandlordCard'
  >;
}

export type AssembleOpts = PoolOpts;

export interface AssembledAnchor {
  ref: AnchorRef;
  record: ContactItem | UnitItem;
  /** IR7: a tenant's name, else its contactId; a property's label, else NO_ADDRESS_LABEL (tenantDisplay / propertyDisplay). */
  display: string;
  card: Card;
  missing: MissingFlag[];
  anchorNotes: AnchorNote[];
  /** The anchor's half of every pair's fingerprints (spec D9 cardChanged). */
  fingerprint: string;
  /** Property anchor: its facts (every candidate carries the same). Tenant anchor: null. */
  propertyFacts: PropertyFacts | null;
  /** Property anchor: its recorded authorities mapped. Tenant anchor: both empty. */
  authorities: AuthorityMapping;
}

interface CandidateBase {
  tenantId: string;
  unitId: string;
  /** The candidate record's id: the contactId (property anchor) or the unitId (tenant anchor). */
  candidateId: string;
  /** IR7: tenantDisplay / propertyDisplay - always a string; never sent to the model. */
  display: string;
  record: ContactItem | UnitItem;
  /** Property anchor only: hasSmsConsent, shown by B3/B4; never a pool rule. */
  hasConsent?: boolean;
  /** Tenant anchor only: the property's Priority switch; read here, never sent to the model. */
  priority?: boolean;
}

export interface VerifiedCandidate extends CandidateBase {
  unverified: false;
  card: Card;
  missing: MissingFlag[];
  pairHistory: PairHistory;
  fingerprints: CardFingerprints;
  /** The pair's property's facts (the cap and the flag check read them). */
  propertyFacts: PropertyFacts;
}

/** Spec D2.3: a candidate whose OWN card reads did not complete - never read as "not on file". */
export interface UnverifiedCandidate extends CandidateBase {
  unverified: true;
  card: null;
  missing: null;
  pairHistory: null;
  fingerprints: null;
  /** The anchor's facts for a property anchor; null for a tenant anchor. */
  propertyFacts: PropertyFacts | null;
}

export type AssembledCandidate = VerifiedCandidate | UnverifiedCandidate;

export interface AssembledRanking {
  ok: true;
  direction: Direction;
  anchor: AssembledAnchor;
  /** Pool order; an unverified candidate stays in its place. */
  candidates: AssembledCandidate[];
  /** Every listed seen home of every tenant card, by first reference in pool order. */
  homes: Map<string, SeenHomeCard>;
  unverifiedCount: number;
}

export interface AnchorUnreadable {
  ok: false;
  reason: 'anchor_unreadable';
  message: string;
  /**
   * PR38 / PR43: set when the anchor's own reads fail AFTER its pool was
   * computed (a tenant anchor's seen set; a property anchor's landlord read,
   * switch on) - the pool's candidate ids in pool order (unitIds, or
   * contactIds), so the job (S5) records each as notScored `unreadable`.
   * Absent when no pool was computed.
   */
  candidateIds?: string[];
}

export type AssembleResult = AssembledRanking | PoolFailure | AnchorUnreadable;

export const ASSEMBLE_MESSAGES = {
  anchorUnreadable: 'This record could not be read in full. Try again.',
} as const;

type Settled<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; err: unknown };

async function settle<T>(work: Promise<T>): Promise<Settled<T>> {
  try {
    return { ok: true, value: await work };
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, err };
  }
}

/** The landlords of record of `units`, one complete batch read (switch on only). */
async function readLandlords(
  units: readonly UnitItem[],
  contacts: Pick<ContactsRepo, 'getManyByIds'>,
): Promise<ReadonlyMap<string, ContactItem>> {
  const ids = [
    ...new Set(
      units.flatMap((unit) => (typeof unit.landlordId === 'string' && unit.landlordId.length > 0 ? [unit.landlordId] : [])),
    ),
  ].sort();
  if (ids.length === 0) return new Map();
  return contacts.getManyByIds(ids, { requireComplete: true });
}

/** IR7: a tenant's display - its name, else its contactId (the id never reaches the model). */
export function tenantDisplay(contact: ContactItem): string {
  return contactDisplayName(contact) ?? contact.contactId;
}

/** IR7: a property's display - its label, else the no-address placeholder (PR23). */
export function propertyDisplay(unit: UnitItem): string {
  return propertyLabel(unit) ?? NO_ADDRESS_LABEL;
}

export interface CreateAssembleDepsOpts extends Pick<RepoDeps, 'env' | 'doc'> {
  config: AppConfig;
  logger: Logger;
}

/**
 * IR9: the production deps of the gatherer - the contacts, units, placements,
 * listing sends and tours repos and the organization names service, all on
 * the given env / doc (the WI18 test runs on a throwaway TABLE_PREFIX). The
 * job (S5 jobWiring.ts) and the read (S6) both build their deps here.
 */
export function createAssembleDeps(opts: CreateAssembleDepsOpts): AssembleDeps {
  const repo: RepoDeps = {
    logger: opts.logger,
    ...(opts.env !== undefined && { env: opts.env }),
    ...(opts.doc !== undefined && { doc: opts.doc }),
  };
  return {
    contacts: createContactsRepo(repo),
    units: createUnitsRepo(repo),
    placements: createPlacementsRepo(repo),
    listingSends: createListingSendsRepo(repo),
    tours: createToursRepo(repo),
    orgNames: createOrgNamesService({ orgListRepo: createOrgListRepo(repo), logger: opts.logger }),
    config: opts.config,
    logger: opts.logger,
  };
}

async function readLandlordOf(
  unit: UnitItem,
  contacts: Pick<ContactsRepo, 'getManyByIds'>,
  landlordCard: boolean,
): Promise<ContactItem | null> {
  if (!landlordCard) return null;
  return (await readLandlords([unit], contacts)).get(unit.landlordId) ?? null;
}

/**
 * Spec D2.3: one tenant card's inputs - one listByContact, one listByTenant,
 * ONE units batch read for the whole seen set (requireComplete: an
 * unprocessed key THROWS, never reads as "not on file") and, switch on, one
 * batch read of those units' landlords. Throws on any failed read; the caller
 * scopes the failure to this card.
 */
export async function readTenantInputs(
  tenantId: string,
  deps: Pick<AssembleDeps, 'contacts' | 'units' | 'listingSends' | 'tours'>,
  landlordCard: boolean,
): Promise<TenantReads> {
  const [sends, tours] = await Promise.all([deps.listingSends.listByContact(tenantId), deps.tours.listByTenant(tenantId)]);
  const ids = seenUnitIds(sends, tours);
  const units: ReadonlyMap<string, UnitItem> =
    ids.length === 0 ? new Map() : await deps.units.getManyByIds(ids, { requireComplete: true });
  const landlords = landlordCard ? await readLandlords([...units.values()], deps.contacts) : new Map<string, ContactItem>();
  return { sends, tours, units, landlords };
}

/**
 * THE gatherer (plan PR3): the pool, the anchor card, every candidate card
 * with its missing flags, pair history, fingerprints and the facts of the
 * pair's property, and the full card of every listed seen home. Candidate
 * reads run with at most RANKING_READ_CONCURRENCY in flight. A candidate
 * whose own reads fail is returned in place, `unverified`; a failure of the
 * anchor's own reads is `anchor_unreadable`; a pool failure passes through.
 * Any other error (the pool's list reads) propagates to the caller.
 */
export async function assembleRanking(anchor: AnchorRef, opts: AssembleOpts, deps: AssembleDeps): Promise<AssembleResult> {
  const pool = await computePool(anchor, opts, deps);
  if (!pool.ok) return pool;
  const ctx: SideCtx = {
    now: opts.now,
    seenMax: deps.config.rankingSeenMax,
    orgEntries: pool.orgEntries,
    landlordCard: deps.config.rankingLandlordCard,
  };
  const limit = deps.config.rankingReadConcurrency;
  const unreadable = (err: unknown): AnchorUnreadable => {
    deps.logger?.warn({ anchorKind: anchor.kind, anchorId: anchor.id, err }, 'ranking: the anchor card could not be read');
    return { ok: false, reason: 'anchor_unreadable', message: ASSEMBLE_MESSAGES.anchorUnreadable };
  };
  const unverifiedLog = (candidateId: string, err: unknown): void => {
    deps.logger?.warn(
      { anchorKind: anchor.kind, anchorId: anchor.id, candidateId, err },
      'ranking: a candidate card could not be read; the candidate is unverified',
    );
  };

  if (pool.kind === 'unit') {
    const unit = pool.anchorRecord;
    const landlord = await settle(readLandlordOf(unit, deps.contacts, ctx.landlordCard));
    if (!landlord.ok) {
      return { ...unreadable(landlord.err), candidateIds: pool.candidates.map((contact) => contact.contactId) };
    }
    const anchorSide = buildPropertySide(unit, { orgEntries: ctx.orgEntries, landlordCard: ctx.landlordCard, landlord: landlord.value });
    const results = await mapWithConcurrency(pool.candidates, limit, async (contact) => {
      const base = {
        tenantId: contact.contactId,
        unitId: unit.unitId,
        candidateId: contact.contactId,
        display: tenantDisplay(contact),
        record: contact,
        hasConsent: hasSmsConsent(contact),
      };
      const reads = await settle(readTenantInputs(contact.contactId, deps, ctx.landlordCard));
      if (!reads.ok) {
        unverifiedLog(contact.contactId, reads.err);
        const candidate: UnverifiedCandidate = {
          ...base,
          unverified: true,
          card: null,
          missing: null,
          pairHistory: null,
          fingerprints: null,
          propertyFacts: anchorSide.facts,
        };
        return { candidate, homes: new Map<string, SeenHomeCard>() };
      }
      const side = buildTenantSide(contact, reads.value, ctx);
      const pairHistory = pairHistoryOf(side.seen.find((home) => home.unitId === unit.unitId), opts.now);
      const candidate: VerifiedCandidate = {
        ...base,
        unverified: false,
        card: side.card,
        missing: side.missing,
        pairHistory,
        fingerprints: {
          tenantCard: side.fingerprint,
          unitCard: anchorSide.fingerprint,
          pairHistory: pairHistoryFingerprint(pairHistory),
        },
        propertyFacts: anchorSide.facts,
      };
      return { candidate, homes: side.homes };
    });
    const homes = new Map<string, SeenHomeCard>();
    for (const result of results) {
      for (const [unitId, home] of result.homes) if (!homes.has(unitId)) homes.set(unitId, home);
    }
    const candidates: AssembledCandidate[] = results.map((result) => result.candidate);
    return {
      ok: true,
      direction: 'tenants_for_property',
      anchor: {
        ref: anchor,
        record: unit,
        display: propertyDisplay(unit),
        card: anchorSide.card,
        missing: anchorSide.missing,
        anchorNotes: pool.anchorNotes,
        fingerprint: anchorSide.fingerprint,
        propertyFacts: anchorSide.facts,
        authorities: pool.authorities,
      },
      candidates,
      homes,
      unverifiedCount: candidates.filter((candidate) => candidate.unverified).length,
    };
  }

  const anchorTenant = pool.anchorRecord;
  const anchorReads = await settle(readTenantInputs(anchorTenant.contactId, deps, ctx.landlordCard));
  if (!anchorReads.ok) {
    return { ...unreadable(anchorReads.err), candidateIds: pool.candidates.map((unit) => unit.unitId) };
  }
  const anchorSide = buildTenantSide(anchorTenant, anchorReads.value, ctx);
  const candidates = await mapWithConcurrency(pool.candidates, limit, async (unit): Promise<AssembledCandidate> => {
    const base = {
      tenantId: anchorTenant.contactId,
      unitId: unit.unitId,
      candidateId: unit.unitId,
      display: propertyDisplay(unit),
      record: unit,
      priority: unit.priority === true,
    };
    const landlord = await settle(readLandlordOf(unit, deps.contacts, ctx.landlordCard));
    if (!landlord.ok) {
      unverifiedLog(unit.unitId, landlord.err);
      return { ...base, unverified: true, card: null, missing: null, pairHistory: null, fingerprints: null, propertyFacts: null };
    }
    const side = buildPropertySide(unit, { orgEntries: ctx.orgEntries, landlordCard: ctx.landlordCard, landlord: landlord.value });
    const pairHistory = pairHistoryOf(anchorSide.seen.find((home) => home.unitId === unit.unitId), opts.now);
    return {
      ...base,
      unverified: false,
      card: side.card,
      missing: side.missing,
      pairHistory,
      fingerprints: {
        tenantCard: anchorSide.fingerprint,
        unitCard: side.fingerprint,
        pairHistory: pairHistoryFingerprint(pairHistory),
      },
      propertyFacts: side.facts,
    };
  });
  return {
    ok: true,
    direction: 'properties_for_tenant',
    anchor: {
      ref: anchor,
      record: anchorTenant,
      display: tenantDisplay(anchorTenant),
      card: anchorSide.card,
      missing: anchorSide.missing,
      anchorNotes: pool.anchorNotes,
      fingerprint: anchorSide.fingerprint,
      propertyFacts: null,
      authorities: pool.authorities,
    },
    candidates,
    homes: anchorSide.homes,
    unverifiedCount: candidates.filter((candidate) => candidate.unverified).length,
  };
}

/**
 * FB4 (PR16): the anchor's missing flags for a pool over the ceiling (the
 * read's anchor block), from what the PoolFailure carries - a tenant
 * anchor's tenantMissing; a property anchor's propertyMissing with the
 * pool's organization list and, switch on, its landlord (read here). [] for
 * any other failure. THROWS when the landlord read cannot finish: the
 * anchor's own read, so the read answers 503 (PR17).
 */
export async function poolTooLargeMissing(
  failure: PoolFailure,
  deps: Pick<AssembleDeps, 'contacts' | 'config'>,
): Promise<MissingFlag[]> {
  const found = failure.anchor;
  if (failure.reason !== 'pool_too_large' || found === undefined) return [];
  if (found.kind === 'tenant') return tenantMissing(found.record);
  const landlordCard = deps.config.rankingLandlordCard;
  const landlord = await readLandlordOf(found.record, deps.contacts, landlordCard);
  return propertyMissing(found.record, { orgEntries: failure.orgEntries ?? [], landlordCard, landlord });
}

/**
 * IR9: each property's CURRENT-card facts, for the run detail's open-flag
 * check (S6): one complete units read for the distinct ids and, switch on,
 * one landlord read, then propertyFacts. A unit the complete read did not
 * find is absent; an incomplete read THROWS (the caller scopes the failure).
 * The facts read no authority mapping, so no organization list is read.
 */
export async function loadPropertyFacts(
  unitIds: readonly string[],
  deps: Pick<AssembleDeps, 'contacts' | 'units' | 'config'>,
): Promise<Map<string, PropertyFacts>> {
  const ids = [...new Set(unitIds)].sort();
  const out = new Map<string, PropertyFacts>();
  if (ids.length === 0) return out;
  const units = await deps.units.getManyByIds(ids, { requireComplete: true });
  const landlordCard = deps.config.rankingLandlordCard;
  const landlords = landlordCard ? await readLandlords([...units.values()], deps.contacts) : new Map<string, ContactItem>();
  for (const [unitId, unit] of units) {
    out.set(unitId, propertyFacts(unit, { orgEntries: [], landlordCard, landlord: landlordOf(unit, landlords) }));
  }
  return out;
}
```

agent runs the compile check against a model (PR1).

### Contradictions

C1. `promptFingerprint` - spec D4 says "sha256 of the system text";
extraction's fingerprint is the first 12 hex of sha256 over the system
prompt AND the schema (`app/src/services/extraction/prompt.ts:212-219`).
Resolution (PR18, departs from spec D4's text; listed for Cameron):
`rankingPromptFingerprint({ landlordCard })` is the FULL 64-hex sha256 over
the system text, one newline, and the stable JSON (keys sorted,
`stableJson` in prompt.ts) of the schema sent on that call - so the two
landlord-switch states have two fingerprints. RUNBOOK "Changing a
structured-output schema" (S4.10) says a change to the ranking schema's
enums bumps `RUBRIC_VERSION`, which marks matches out of date.

C2. WI22 / spec D5 "the plan confirms each [free-text field] is stored as a
string on `UnitItem`". The tree (`app/src/repos/unitsRepo.ts`): `utilities?:
string` (:449), `accessibility?: string` (:451), `notes?: string` (:457),
`lease_terms?: string` (:464), `tour_process?: string` (:498),
`application_process?: string` (:507), `evictions_notes?: string` (:519),
`qualifications?: string` (:525), `pet_fee?: string` (:529),
`deposit_notes?: string` (:535) - but `pets?: string | boolean` (:471), a
legacy bare boolean. Resolution: the unlawful-flag rule reads the CARD's
text (`propertyFacts(...).freeTextByField`, S3), and the card reads `pets`
through `unitItemValue` (`app/src/lib/requirements.ts:188-198`): a legacy
`false` reads as blank details text (a flag on it is dropped), a legacy
`true` as "Allowed". No code here reads `UnitItem.pets` directly. The S4
report quotes these eleven lines.

C3. The landlord twins of the flag-field enum. Spec D5 says "their
landlord-default twins as `landlord:<key>`"; spec D2.1 says the landlord
defaults are the landlord's requirement values (credit and income left out)
plus the landlord contact's `notes`. `lease_terms`, `application_process`,
`utilities` and `accessibility` have no landlord field
(`REQUIREMENT_LANDLORD_KEYS`, requirements.ts:119-121, holds only the 15
requirement keys). Resolution: the twins are `landlord:<each of the 13
reportable requirement keys>` plus `landlord:notes` (14); the unlawful
subset of the twins is the seven free-text ones
(`landlord:qualifications`, `landlord:evictions_notes`, `landlord:pets`,
`landlord:pet_fee`, `landlord:deposit_notes`, `landlord:tour_process`,
`landlord:notes`). Enum sizes: 18 with the switch off, 32 with it on.

C4. "unknown enum values dropped" for a reason. Resolution: a reason whose
`source` is not in the enum is DROPPED (never re-labelled `other`), and the
cut to three counts only valid reasons (a bad first reason does not cost a
good fourth one its slot). The same order for `unknowns` (cut to five after
the empties are dropped).

C5. A returned candidate whose `score` is not a finite number. The spec is
silent; charter 7.4 forbids a guessed score. Resolution: that candidate gets
NO parsed result (listed in `unscoredHandles`), exactly like a missing one.

C6. Refusal details. The skill docs describe `stop_details` on a refusal;
the installed SDK version (`@anthropic-ai/sdk` ^0.129.0, app/package.json)
is not inspectable here (no node_modules) and extraction never reads it
(`app/src/adapters/extraction.ts:349-354`). Resolution: the driver reads
only `stop_reason`, as extraction does.

C7. Request shape vs the installed SDK's types. Extraction already sends
`output_config: { format: ... }` and `thinking: { type: 'between_tools' }`
(extraction.ts:306-313), so `output_config` and a newer thinking type are
typed. `output_config.effort` and `thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }` are not
used anywhere in the tree yet. Resolution: S4.9 sends both exactly as spec
D6 states. Whether SDK 0.129 types `effort` (and its five levels, S2's
`RankingEffort` union includes `xhigh` and `max`), `'adaptive'` and
`APIConnectionTimeoutError` is UNVERIFIED here (no node_modules). If
`npm run typecheck` reports any of them, STOP and report it to the
orchestrator as a finding that QUOTES the exact tsc output (file, line,
message) - an error naming only `'xhigh'` / `'max'` points at S2's union, not
at a missing feature, and the planner decides (FB24); never cast through
`unknown`.

C8. `maxRetries: 1` (spec D6) means the SDK retries a timed-out call once,
so one call's wall clock is bounded at 2 x `RANKING_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (240 s
at the default), not 120 s. Accepted as written; the timeout failure
message says "one retry included"; the lease renewal (S5) runs on its own
timer.

C9. Where the supported-model check stops startup. Spec D6: "any other
`AI_RANKING_MODEL` stops startup". S2's draft puts the set
(`RANKING_SUPPORTED_MODELS`), the refusal, the unpriced-model refusal and
`RankingEffort` in `lib/config.ts` and says S4 "may re-assert
`RANKING_SUPPORTED_MODELS` but must not re-define it". Resolution: S4
imports all three from `lib/config.ts` (never re-defines them);
`createRankingDriver` RE-ASSERTS the supported set for driver `anthropic`
(a second guard for a caller that builds settings without `loadConfig`,
such as the counterfactual script).

C10. The anchor property in a property anchor's seen sets. Spec D4 makes an
exception only for a seen home that is "also a candidate". Resolution
(PR20): a properties-seen entry names its home under the key `home`; in the
call a seen home that is the property ANCHOR is `home: "anchor"` (written
once, as the anchor card), one that is a candidate is its `c` handle, and
any other is its `h` handle in `homesSeen`. For a property anchor the anchor
unit is every candidate's `unitId` (the pair's property), so
`buildRankingBatch` needs no extra input. The rubric's THE INPUT section
says so; S4.7's tests cover all three references and that no `unitId`
reaches the user text.

C11. Where the price-table default lives. PR4 makes `aiPriceTable` a config
field; the brief puts `AI_PRICE_TABLE` in `cost.ts`; S2's draft defines
`DEFAULT_AI_PRICE_TABLE`, `AiPrice` and `AiPriceTable` in `lib/config.ts`.
Resolution: one home, S2's. `cost.ts` holds only the formula and takes the
table as an argument (`costUsd(model, usage, priceTable)`, the argument
order S5's draft calls it with); S4.2 pins the formula against config's
default table.

C12. Names S5's draft expects (its section 9 "What S5 needs from S4"):
`buildRankingPrompt(...)` returning a `RankingPrompt` with `batchInput`,
`userText`, `promptFingerprint`, `handles` (with `display`) and
`snapshotOf(candidateId)`; `RankingCallMeta`; `RankingBatchInput`
importable from `driverTypes.ts`; `createRankingDriver(config, logger)`;
`ParsedRanking` constructible as `{ byHandle, droppedUnlawfulFlags }`.
Resolution: S4 provides each. `buildRankingBatch` stays the core builder
(the counterfactual script calls it without a display); `buildRankingPrompt`
wraps it and needs two fields S5's call does not yet pass, `batchIndex` and
`landlordCard` (the schema and the parse rule depend on the switch) - PR19:
S5's call passes `batchIndex` and `landlordCard: deps.config.rankingLandlordCard`. `createRankingDriver` takes the
config fields by their AppConfig names (a `Pick<AppConfig, ...>`), so S5
passes `config` itself. The parse output's three handle lists are optional
in the type (always set by `parseRankingText`) so a stub output of
`{ byHandle, droppedUnlawfulFlags }` type-checks; `RankingCallMeta.promptFingerprint`
is optional for the same reason (every S4 driver sets it).

C13. Plan review rounds 1-3 (PR29 as amended by PR40 and PR45, PR31-PR33, PR41,
PR44, FB23-FB26, FA3, R2F3, R2F12-R2F14), applied here: `capOf` suppresses
an ACCOMMODATION by requirement item through S3's `requirementItemOfField`
(with `qualifications` joining every cap-eligible item, for accommodation
only: PR45) and an open UNLAWFUL flag only on its own field (S4.1); the field constants come from S3's
`cardFields.ts` and S4 defines none (S4.1, S4.3, S4.4); the worked examples
carry the production `missing` labels, seen entries with `label`, and all
three home references, checked by S4.6's tests; S4.11 pins the prompt bytes
to their versions - the rendered system text, the rubric, the rendered
examples, the user-message framing and both schemas as sent (R2F3); an
accommodation flag on any property-card field in the enum is kept (PR44,
FA5 reversed; only an item field affects the cap); the rubric matches the
cards, scopes eligibility to candidates (R2F14), says card text is data and
gives ONE accommodation instruction: raise it on every field that states
the covered requirement and list none of them failed (PR41, PR45) (S4.5); the examples test calls S3's
`propertyMissing` / `tenantMissing` (R2F13); the fake's labels resolve in
the driver constructors (S4.8, R2F12); the
compile check's opus limit is in RUNBOOK (S4.10); the STOP rule quotes the
tsc error (C7); the S4.12 greps match only what they mean to.

### Cross-slice notes (for the planner)

Exports S4 adds that later slices use (exact signatures):

Create `app/src/services/ranking/bands.ts`:

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D9 (charter 8): the band a score falls in. Starting values,
// tunable without a prompt change; changing them re-ranks nothing (bands are
// derived on read, never stored). Pure, no imports.

export type Band = 'strong' | 'good' | 'possible' | 'weak';

/** The lowest score of each band above Weak. */
export const BAND_FLOORS: Readonly<{ strong: number; good: number; possible: number }> = Object.freeze({
  strong: 80,
  good: 60,
  possible: 40,
});

/** Best band first: the read sorts by this order (spec D9). */
export const BAND_ORDER: readonly Band[] = Object.freeze(['strong', 'good', 'possible', 'weak'] as const);

export function bandOf(score: number): Band {
  if (score >= BAND_FLOORS.strong) return 'strong';
  if (score >= BAND_FLOORS.good) return 'good';
  if (score >= BAND_FLOORS.possible) return 'possible';
  return 'weak';
}
```

Create `app/src/services/ranking/cap.ts`:

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D9 (charter 7.4): the Weak cap, computed in code from the
// model's own report. THE one cap function (plan PR7, WI13): the read, the
// run's cappedAtRun and the counterfactual check all call capOf; none
// re-implements it. Pure.
//
// A pair is capped when its failedRequirements holds a CAP-ELIGIBLE key that
// (a) is recorded on that property's current card (a landlord default counts
// when the landlord card switch is on - the caller passes plain keys),
// (b) whose requirement ITEM carries none of the same pair's accommodation
//     flags (PR29: no_pets, pets and pet_fee are the one Pets item, so an
//     accommodation on no_pets covers a failed pets; PR45: for accommodation
//     only, qualifications joins every cap-eligible item, so an accommodation
//     on a Pets or Evictions key covers a failed qualifications and one on
//     qualifications covers a failed key of either item - the same rule is
//     often written both as a checkbox and in the qualifications text), and
// (c) whose own FIELD has no open unlawful flag on that property (PR40: an
//     unlawful flag on pets text does not lift the lawful No pets checkbox;
//     spec D9 / D10 "that field caps no pair").
// A flag on `landlord:<key>` counts as a flag on `<key>` (spec D2.1). An
// accommodation on a field of no item (notes, lease_terms, ...) suppresses
// nothing. Credit, income, move-in costs and touring never cap: they are not
// cap-eligible keys.
import { LANDLORD_FIELD_PREFIX, requirementItemOfField } from './cardFields.js';

export const CAP_ELIGIBLE_KEYS = Object.freeze([
  'no_evictions_on_program',
  'evictions_notes',
  'qualifications',
  'no_pets',
  'pets',
] as const);

export const CAP_REASON = 'requirement not met' as const;

const CAP_ELIGIBLE: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(CAP_ELIGIBLE_KEYS);

/** `landlord:<key>` -> `<key>`; any other field unchanged. */
export function baseField(field: string): string {
  return field.startsWith(LANDLORD_FIELD_PREFIX) ? field.slice(LANDLORD_FIELD_PREFIX.length) : field;
}

/** The fields of one flag kind, in the order given. */
export function flagFieldsOfKind(
  flags: readonly { kind: string; field: string }[],
  kind: 'unlawful' | 'accommodation',
): string[] {
  return flags.filter((flag) => flag.kind === kind).map((flag) => flag.field);
}

export interface CapInput {
  failedRequirements: readonly string[];
  accommodationFields: readonly string[];
  recordedRequirementKeys: readonly string[];
  openUnlawfulFields: readonly string[];
}

export interface CapResult {
  capped: boolean;
  capReason: typeof CAP_REASON | null;
}

/** The requirement items the given (plain or landlord:) fields belong to (S3's requirementItemOfField, PR29); a field of no item adds nothing. */
function itemsOf(fields: readonly string[]): Set<string> {
  const items = new Set<string>();
  for (const field of fields) {
    const item = requirementItemOfField(field);
    if (item !== undefined) items.add(item);
  }
  return items;
}

/** The items of the cap-eligible keys (Evictions, qualifications, Pets). */
const CAP_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS: ReadonlySet<string> = itemsOf(CAP_ELIGIBLE_KEYS);
const QUALIFICATIONS_ITEM = 'qualifications';

/** PR29 + PR45: does an accommodation on `accommodated` items cover a failure of `item`? */
function accommodationCovers(item: string, accommodated: ReadonlySet<string>): boolean {
  if (accommodated.has(item)) return true;
  if (!CAP_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS.has(item)) return false;
  if (item === QUALIFICATIONS_ITEM) return [...accommodated].some((a) => CAP_ELIGIBLE_ITEMS.has(a));
  return accommodated.has(QUALIFICATIONS_ITEM);
}

export function capOf(input: CapInput): CapResult {
  const recorded = new Set(input.recordedRequirementKeys.map(baseField));
  const accommodatedItems = itemsOf(input.accommodationFields);
  const unlawfulFields = new Set(input.openUnlawfulFields.map(baseField));
  for (const raw of input.failedRequirements) {
    const key = baseField(raw);
    if (!CAP_ELIGIBLE.has(key)) continue;
    if (!recorded.has(key)) continue;
    const item = requirementItemOfField(key);
    if (item !== undefined && accommodationCovers(item, accommodatedItems)) continue;
    if (unlawfulFields.has(key)) continue;
    return { capped: true, capReason: CAP_REASON };
  }
  return { capped: false, capReason: null };
}
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D6: the dollar cost of one ranking call. The price table
// (dollars per million input / output tokens per model id) is config's:
// DEFAULT_AI_PRICE_TABLE in lib/config.ts (the Claude API model table as of
// 2026-10-06, confirmed by Cameron at the spec gate), replaced whole by
// AI_PRICE_TABLE (S2). The caller passes it in. Prompt caching is off
// (charter 14), so cache-read tokens are recorded on the run but not priced.
// Pure: a type-only import.
import type { AiPrice } from '../../lib/config.js';

type PriceTable = Readonly<Record<string, Readonly<AiPrice>>>;

/** The model ids the fake and console drivers stamp: they call nothing and cost nothing. */
const UNBILLED_MODELS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['fake', 'console']);

export function priceOf(priceTable: PriceTable, model: string): Readonly<AiPrice> | undefined {
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(priceTable, model) ? priceTable[model] : undefined;
}

/**
 * in * inputTokens / 1e6 + out * outputTokens / 1e6, rounded to 1e-6 dollars.
 * Zero for the fake and console drivers and for a call that carried no usage.
 * Throws for a billed model with no price: startup refuses that config (S2),
 * so reaching it is a programming error.
 */
export function costUsd(
  model: string,
  usage: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number } | undefined,
  priceTable: PriceTable,
): number {
  if (usage === undefined || UNBILLED_MODELS.has(model)) return 0;
  const price = priceOf(priceTable, model);
  if (price === undefined) throw new Error(`no price for model ${model} in AI_PRICE_TABLE`);
  const dollars = (price.in * usage.inputTokens) / 1e6 + (price.out * usage.outputTokens) / 1e6;
  return Math.round(dollars * 1e6) / 1e6;
}
```

```ts
// schema into a grammar with a size limit no offline test can see (B1: eight
// named objects compiled, twelve failed). This test pins the shape so a later
// edit that grows it fails HERE first (plan WI21); the real compile is

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import type { UnitItem } from '../src/repos/unitsRepo.js';

  EXCLUDED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS,
  LANDLORD_DEFAULT_KEYS,

  'minimum', 'maximum', 'exclusiveMinimum', 'exclusiveMaximum', 'multipleOf',
  'minLength', 'maxLength', 'minItems', 'maxItems', 'minProperties', 'maxProperties',
];

function walk(node: unknown, visit: (obj: Node, path: string) => void, path = 'schema'): void {
  if (Array.isArray(node)) {
    node.forEach((child, i) => walk(child, visit, `${path}[${i}]`));
    return;
  }
  if (node !== null && typeof node === 'object') {
    const obj = node as Node;
    visit(obj, path);
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(obj)) walk(value, visit, `${path}.${key}`);
  }
}

  it('an unlawful flag may name only a free-text field (and its landlord twin when on)', () => {
    expect(unlawfulFieldsFor(false)).toEqual([...PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS]);
    expect(unlawfulFieldsFor(true)).toEqual([
      ...PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS,
      'landlord:evictions_notes', 'landlord:qualifications', 'landlord:pets', 'landlord:pet_fee',
      'landlord:deposit_notes', 'landlord:tour_process', 'landlord:notes',
    ]);
    for (const checkbox of ['no_pets', 'no_evictions_on_program', 'deposit_one_month', 'deposit_flexible', 'deposit', 'application_fee', 'tour_type']) {
      expect(unlawfulFieldsFor(true)).not.toContain(checkbox);
    }
  });
});

// PR33 / WI22: the field constants live in cardFields.ts (S3); the schema
// derives its enums from them. Tie them to the card: every free-text field
// and every reportable requirement key is an INCLUDED property-card field, and
// every free-text field but the legacy `pets` (read through unitItemValue,
// plan C2) is string-typed on UnitItem - the `satisfies` below fails
// `npm run typecheck` (vitest strips types) if one changes type.
type FreeTextField = 'notes' | 'lease_terms' | 'application_process' | 'qualifications' | 'evictions_notes'
  | 'pet_fee' | 'deposit_notes' | 'tour_process' | 'utilities' | 'accessibility';
const STRING_TYPED_FREE_TEXT = {
  notes: true, lease_terms: true, application_process: true, qualifications: true, evictions_notes: true,
  pet_fee: true, deposit_notes: true, tour_process: true, utilities: true, accessibility: true,
} as const satisfies { [K in FreeTextField]: UnitItem[K] extends string | undefined ? true : never };

describe('the card-field constants are the card\'s (PR33)', () => {
  it('every free-text field and every reportable requirement key is an included property-card field', () => {
    const registry = PROPERTY_CARD_FIELDS as Readonly<Record<string, { use: string }>>;
    for (const field of [...PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS, ...RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS]) {
      expect(registry[field]?.use, field).toBe('include');
    }
  });

  it('the free-text list is the string-typed set plus the legacy pets (WI22)', () => {
    expect([...PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS].sort()).toEqual([...Object.keys(STRING_TYPED_FREE_TEXT), 'pets'].sort());
  });
});
```
