#### Step 3 - implementation

Create `app/src/services/ranking/schema.ts`:

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D5 (charter 7.4): the ranking call's structured-output
// schema and its enums. Extraction's schema discipline: every key required
// (zero optional parameters), additionalProperties:false on every object,
// sentinels for none (empty arrays), no numeric or length bounds (the parser
// clamps and cuts in code, parse.ts).
//
// GRAMMAR SIZE: the API compiles the schema into a grammar with a size limit
// no offline test can see (WP1 B1: eight named objects compiled, twelve
// failed). This schema has five object nodes - the root, the candidate, the
// reason (inlined twice, for and against) and the flag - and
// test/rankingSchema.test.ts pins that. After ANY change here, Cameron runs
// app/scripts/extraction-schema-compile-check.ts (both `ranking` variants;
// RUNBOOK "Changing a structured-output schema").
// PR33: the free-text field list, the reportable requirement keys and the
// landlord prefix have ONE home, S3's cardFields.ts; this file derives the
// enums from them and defines none of its own.
import {
  LANDLORD_DEFAULT_KEYS,
  LANDLORD_FIELD_PREFIX,
  PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS,
  RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS,
} from './cardFields.js';

/** Where a reason came from (spec D5). */
export const RANKING_SOURCES = Object.freeze([
  'voucher_size',
  'authority',
  'rent',
  'area',
  'pets',
  'evictions',
  'accessibility',
  'requirements',
  'preferences',
  'notes',
  'staff_notes',
  'feedback',
  'history',
  'recency',
  'property_details',
  'other',
] as const);

export type RankingSource = (typeof RANKING_SOURCES)[number];

const FLAG_FIELDS_OFF: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
  ...RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS,
  ...PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS.filter((field) => !RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS.includes(field)),
]);
const FLAG_FIELDS_ON: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
  ...FLAG_FIELDS_OFF,
  ...LANDLORD_DEFAULT_KEYS.map((field) => `${LANDLORD_FIELD_PREFIX}${field}`),
]);
const UNLAWFUL_FIELDS_OFF: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([...PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS]);
const UNLAWFUL_FIELDS_ON: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
  ...PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS,
  ...LANDLORD_DEFAULT_KEYS.filter((field) => PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS.includes(field)).map(
    (field) => `${LANDLORD_FIELD_PREFIX}${field}`,
  ),
]);

/** Every property card field a flag can name, for one state of RANKING_LANDLORD_CARD. */
export function flagFieldsFor(landlordCard: boolean): readonly string[] {
  return landlordCard ? FLAG_FIELDS_ON : FLAG_FIELDS_OFF;
}

/** The fields an `unlawful` flag may name, for one state of RANKING_LANDLORD_CARD. */
export function unlawfulFieldsFor(landlordCard: boolean): readonly string[] {
  return landlordCard ? UNLAWFUL_FIELDS_ON : UNLAWFUL_FIELDS_OFF;
}

function reasonSchema(): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    type: 'object',
    additionalProperties: false,
    properties: {
      text: { type: 'string' },
      source: { type: 'string', enum: [...RANKING_SOURCES] },
    },
    required: ['text', 'source'],
  };
}

function buildSchema(landlordCard: boolean): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    type: 'object',
    additionalProperties: false,
    properties: {
      candidates: {
        type: 'array',
        items: {
          type: 'object',
          additionalProperties: false,
          properties: {
            // The per-call handle (c1, c2, ...); ids are never on the cards.
            candidateId: { type: 'string' },
            // 0-100; clamped and rounded in parse.ts (no bounds here).
            score: { type: 'integer' },
            for: { type: 'array', items: reasonSchema() },
            against: { type: 'array', items: reasonSchema() },
            unknowns: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
            failedRequirements: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string', enum: [...RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS] } },
            // The schema cannot tie `field` to `kind` without another named
            // object, so code enforces "unlawful names a free-text field"
            // (parse.ts).
            fairHousingFlags: {
              type: 'array',
              items: {
                type: 'object',
                additionalProperties: false,
                properties: {
                  kind: { type: 'string', enum: ['unlawful', 'accommodation'] },
                  field: { type: 'string', enum: [...flagFieldsFor(landlordCard)] },
                },
                required: ['kind', 'field'],
              },
            },
          },
          required: ['candidateId', 'score', 'for', 'against', 'unknowns', 'failedRequirements', 'fairHousingFlags'],
        },
      },
    },
    required: ['candidates'],
  };
}

const SCHEMA_OFF = buildSchema(false);
const SCHEMA_ON = buildSchema(true);

/** The schema for one state of RANKING_LANDLORD_CARD (the same object every call). */
export function rankingSchema(opts: { landlordCard: boolean }): Record<string, unknown> {
  return opts.landlordCard ? SCHEMA_ON : SCHEMA_OFF;
}
```

#### Step 3 - implementation

Create `app/src/services/ranking/parse.ts`:

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D5 (charter 7.4): parse the ranking call's response text.
// NEVER throws: a whole-output problem returns { ok: false } (the driver
// maps it to failure 'parse', and the batch gets no match for anyone). Per
// candidate:
// - score: a finite number, clamped to 0-100 and rounded; anything else and
//   the candidate gets no result (listed in unscoredHandles; plan C5);
// - for / against: valid reasons only (a known source and non-empty text),
//   each text trimmed and cut to 80 characters, the first three kept (C4);
// - unknowns: non-empty trimmed strings, the first five kept;
// - failedRequirements: the requirement enum only, once each; credit and
//   income keys dropped whatever arrives;
// - fairHousingFlags: kind and field in the enums; an `unlawful` flag whose
//   field is not a free-text field, or holds no text on that pair's property
//   card, is dropped AND counted (droppedUnlawfulFlags); an `accommodation`
//   flag is kept on any enum field (PR44); duplicates once.
// A handle returned twice (every copy discarded), an unknown handle and a
// candidate the model did not return all get no result: a default or
// guessed score is never written.
import { EXCLUDED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS, RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS } from './cardFields.js';
import {
  RANKING_SOURCES,
  flagFieldsFor,
  unlawfulFieldsFor,
  type RankingSource,
} from './schema.js';

export const MAX_REASONS = 3;
export const MAX_REASON_CHARS = 80;
export const MAX_UNKNOWNS = 5;
/** An unknown handle is listed on the run cut to this length (it is model text). */
const MAX_LISTED_HANDLE_CHARS = 20;

export type FlagKind = 'unlawful' | 'accommodation';

export interface RankingReason {
  text: string;
  source: RankingSource;
}

export interface RankingFlag {
  kind: FlagKind;
  field: string;
}

export interface ParsedCandidate {
  score: number;
  for: RankingReason[];
  against: RankingReason[];
  unknowns: string[];
  failedRequirements: string[];
  fairHousingFlags: RankingFlag[];
}

export interface ParsedRanking {
  /** One result per scored handle, in handle (pool) order. */
  byHandle: Map<string, ParsedCandidate>;
  droppedUnlawfulFlags: number;
  // The three lists are ALWAYS set by parseRankingText; optional in the type
  // only so a stub driver's output of { byHandle, droppedUnlawfulFlags }
  // type-checks (plan C12).
  duplicateHandles?: string[];
  unknownHandles?: string[];
  unscoredHandles?: string[];
}

export interface RankingParseContext {
  /** The batch's handles, c1..cn in pool order. */
  handles: readonly string[];
  /** Per handle: the free text of that pair's property card (propertyFacts.freeTextByField). */
  freeTextByHandle: ReadonlyMap<string, Readonly<Record<string, string>>>;
  landlordCard: boolean;
}

export type RankingParseResult = { ok: true; value: ParsedRanking } | { ok: false; message: string };

const SOURCES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(RANKING_SOURCES);
const REQUIREMENTS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS);
const NEVER_REPORTED: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(EXCLUDED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS);

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);
}

function readReasons(raw: unknown): RankingReason[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
  const out: RankingReason[] = [];
  for (const item of raw as unknown[]) {
    if (out.length === MAX_REASONS) break;
    if (!isRecord(item)) continue;
    const source = item['source'];
    const textRaw = item['text'];
    if (typeof source !== 'string' || !SOURCES.has(source)) continue;
    if (typeof textRaw !== 'string') continue;
    const text = textRaw.trim().slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS).trim();
    if (text.length === 0) continue;
    out.push({ text, source: source as RankingSource });
  }
  return out;
}

function readUnknowns(raw: unknown): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const item of raw as unknown[]) {
    if (out.length === MAX_UNKNOWNS) break;
    if (typeof item !== 'string') continue;
    const text = item.trim();
    if (text.length > 0) out.push(text);
  }
  return out;
}

function readFailed(raw: unknown): string[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const item of raw as unknown[]) {
    if (typeof item !== 'string') continue;
    if (NEVER_REPORTED.has(item) || !REQUIREMENTS.has(item)) continue;
    if (!out.includes(item)) out.push(item);
  }
  return out;
}

function readFlags(
  raw: unknown,
  freeText: Readonly<Record<string, string>>,
  landlordCard: boolean,
): { flags: RankingFlag[]; dropped: number } {
  if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return { flags: [], dropped: 0 };
  const allowed = new Set(flagFieldsFor(landlordCard));
  const unlawfulAllowed = new Set(unlawfulFieldsFor(landlordCard));
  const flags: RankingFlag[] = [];
  let dropped = 0;
  for (const item of raw as unknown[]) {
    if (!isRecord(item)) continue;
    const kind = item['kind'];
    const field = item['field'];
    if (kind === 'unlawful') {
      const text = typeof field === 'string' && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(freeText, field) ? freeText[field] : undefined;
      if (typeof field !== 'string' || !unlawfulAllowed.has(field) || typeof text !== 'string' || text.trim().length === 0) {
        dropped += 1;
        continue;
      }
    } else if (kind === 'accommodation') {
      // PR44 (FA5 reversed): an accommodation may name ANY field of the flag
      // enum (spec D5) and is kept as returned - a modification need against
      // `accessibility` or a pets rule in `lease_terms` is a real signal. Only
      // a field of a requirement item affects the cap (cap.ts, PR40). A field
      // outside the enum is dropped.
      if (typeof field !== 'string' || !allowed.has(field)) continue;
    } else {
      continue;
    }
    if (flags.some((flag) => flag.kind === kind && flag.field === field)) continue;
    flags.push({ kind, field });
  }
  return { flags, dropped };
}

export function parseRankingText(text: string, ctx: RankingParseContext): RankingParseResult {
  let root: unknown;
  try {
    root = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    // A fixed message: a SyntaxError's own message can quote the text (PII).
    return { ok: false, message: 'ranking output is not valid JSON' };
  }
  if (!isRecord(root) || !Array.isArray(root['candidates'])) {
    return { ok: false, message: 'ranking output has no candidates list' };
  }
  const known = new Set(ctx.handles);
  const entriesByHandle = new Map<string, Record<string, unknown>[]>();
  const unknownHandles: string[] = [];
  for (const item of root['candidates'] as unknown[]) {
    if (!isRecord(item)) continue;
    const id = item['candidateId'];
    if (typeof id !== 'string') continue;
    const handle = id.trim();
    if (!known.has(handle)) {
      const listed = handle.slice(0, MAX_LISTED_HANDLE_CHARS);
      if (!unknownHandles.includes(listed)) unknownHandles.push(listed);
      continue;
    }
    const list = entriesByHandle.get(handle) ?? [];
    list.push(item);
    entriesByHandle.set(handle, list);
  }
  const byHandle = new Map<string, ParsedCandidate>();
  const duplicateHandles: string[] = [];
  const unscoredHandles: string[] = [];
  let droppedUnlawfulFlags = 0;
  for (const handle of ctx.handles) {
    const list = entriesByHandle.get(handle);
    if (list === undefined) continue;
    if (list.length > 1) {
      duplicateHandles.push(handle);
      continue;
    }
    const item = list[0]!;
    const score = item['score'];
    if (typeof score !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(score)) {
      unscoredHandles.push(handle);
      continue;
    }
    const flags = readFlags(item['fairHousingFlags'], ctx.freeTextByHandle.get(handle) ?? {}, ctx.landlordCard);
    droppedUnlawfulFlags += flags.dropped;
    byHandle.set(handle, {
      score: Math.min(100, Math.max(0, Math.round(score))),
      for: readReasons(item['for']),
      against: readReasons(item['against']),
      unknowns: readUnknowns(item['unknowns']),
      failedRequirements: readFailed(item['failedRequirements']),
      fairHousingFlags: flags.flags,
    });
  }
  return {
    ok: true,
    value: { byHandle, droppedUnlawfulFlags, duplicateHandles, unknownHandles, unscoredHandles },
  };
}
```

Note: in `readFlags`, after the `kind === 'unlawful'` / `'accommodation'`
branches TypeScript narrows `kind` to the two literals and `field` to
`string` at the `push`; if the installed TypeScript does not narrow `field`
through the `continue` paths, write `flags.push({ kind, field: field as string })`
- the runtime guard above already proved it is a string.

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D4 (charter 7.1, 7.2): the ranking rubric, version r1. A .ts
// module, not a Markdown file, so the compiled dist/ carries it (the smoke
// gate proves imports resolve under plain Node). The system prompt is this
// text then the worked examples (prompt.ts), byte-stable for a given pair of
// versions. ANY edit to the text below is a new RUBRIC_VERSION: every match
// records the version it was scored under, and a match scored under another
// version reads out of date (spec D9).
//
// It names the four tenant matching inputs by their list LABELS, because the
// tenant card keys them by label (spec D2.1); test/rankingRubric.test.ts
// fails if a label changes without this text.

export const RUBRIC_VERSION = 'r1';

export const RUBRIC_TEXT = [
  'You score how well housing candidates fit one anchor, for a team that places Housing Choice Voucher holders in homes. Every pair stays visible to staff, whatever you score it.',

  '- One entry per candidate in the input, with candidateId set to that candidate\'s handle (c1, c2, ...). Never skip a candidate, never repeat one, never invent a handle.',
  '- score: a whole number from 0 to 100.',
  '- for and against: up to three reasons each, most important first.',
  '- unknowns: up to five short notes on what you could not judge.',
  '- failedRequirements: the keys of property requirements this tenant fails (rules below).',
  '- fairHousingFlags: the fair housing flags this pair raises (rules below).',
  '- Use an empty list wherever nothing applies.',
  '',
  'WHAT A SCORE MEANS',
  'Scores are ABSOLUTE. They describe the pair against these anchor points, never against the other candidates in the call:',
  '- 100: nothing against, and the tenant\'s preferences are met.',
  '- 80: a strong fit with minor compromises.',
  '- 60: workable, with a real compromise.',
  '- 40: unlikely to work.',
  '- 0: cannot work.',
  'Use the values in between. A 70 must mean the same thing in every call, whoever else is in it. Two equally good candidates get the same score; do not spread scores out to make an order.',
  '',
  'THE INPUT',
  '- anchor: the anchor\'s card, with "missing": the gaps code found on that record.',
  '- homesSeen: every other home that a tenant card in this call lists under propertiesSeen, written once as { handle, label, card }. A propertiesSeen entry names its home in "home": "anchor" means the anchor property itself (its card is the anchor card), a c handle points to that candidate\'s own card, and an h handle points into homesSeen.',
  '- candidates: each with its handle, card, missing and pairHistory.',
  '- A tenant card can hold: the tenant\'s name, current address, voucherSize (bedrooms), housingAuthority, porting, tenure, pets, evictions, status, voucher dates, customFields, the Notes box ("notes"), "staff_notes", "preferences_notes", the inputs "Area preference", "Maximum tenant portion" (whole dollars a month the tenant can pay toward rent), "Accessibility need" and "Preferences and constraints", "lastHeardFrom" (this week, this month, one to three months, older or never) and "propertiesSeen".',

A Notes line that names no home stays in "notes" and bears on every property.',
  '- A property card can hold: address, beds, baths, area, subzone, rent_min, rent_max, final_rent, payment_standard, the move-in costs (deposit, deposit_one_month, deposit_flexible, deposit_notes, application_fee), same_day_rta, utilities (the ones the tenant pays), accessibility, notes, lease_terms, the pets item (no_pets, pets, pet_fee), the evictions item (no_evictions_on_program, evictions_notes), qualifications, touring (tour_type, tour_process), application_process, washer_dryer, status, created_at, voucherSizes (the voucher sizes it accepts, 0 to 4, where 4 means 4 or more bedrooms; voucherSizesInferredFromBeds is true when they come from the bedroom count) and authorities (the housing authorities it accepts; "unmapped" names could not be matched to the organization list). A requirement checkbox (no_pets, no_evictions_on_program, deposit_one_month, deposit_flexible) appears only when it is checked (true); same_day_rta shows its recorded true or false.',

  'DECLINES AND THE MAYBE RULE',
  '- A decline (staff marked the send "Not interested") is a reason against that you weigh; it never forces the Weak range.',
  '- When feedback on that same property says the tenant was unsure (on the fence, maybe, wants to see other homes first), read it as a MAYBE: only a slight reason against, which fades as daysSinceLastSend grows. A clear no in the feedback weighs more.',
  '',
  'FAIR HOUSING',
  '- Protected characteristics NEVER lower a score: race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation and gender identity), national origin, familial status (children, pregnancy, marital status) and disability. Never use a name, an address, a housing authority or a voucher program as a stand-in for any of them, and never give one as a reason against.',
  '- Disability enters only for the tenant\'s benefit: their own accessibility need matched to the home, and an accommodation (below).',
  '- Credit and income are disregarded: a credit or income requirement in ANY field of a property card (qualifications, notes, deposit notes, application process, custom fields, landlord defaults) and a credit or income fact about the tenant wherever it is written (notes, staff notes, custom fields). Never report one failed, never let one lower a score, never give one as a reason. Rent, the payment standard and the "Maximum tenant portion" are NOT credit or income: they stay inputs.',
  '',
  'FAIR HOUSING FLAGS (two kinds, never confused)',
  '- unlawful: a requirement or text on the property that fair housing does not allow for ANY tenant, for example "no kids", "adults only", "no children under 12" or "English speakers only". Name the free-text field that holds it: notes, lease_terms, application_process, qualifications, evictions_notes, pets, pet_fee, deposit_notes, tour_process, utilities or accessibility (landlord:<field> when it is in landlordDefaults). Never name a checkbox: no_pets, no_evictions_on_program, deposit_one_month and deposit_flexible are lawful on their face. Do NOT apply an unlawful requirement: score the pair as if it were absent, never put it in failedRequirements, and add one unknowns note that names the field, for example "qualifications: no-kids rule not applied (fair housing)". Raise the flag on every pair of that property.',
  '- accommodation: a lawful requirement that does not apply to THIS tenant, for example No pets against an assistance animal (a service or support animal) the tenant\'s card records. Raise the accommodation on EVERY field that states the covered requirement, and list none of them failed: No pets checked and repeated in qualifications is an accommodation on no_pets and on qualifications; a pets rule written only in qualifications (for example "No pets of any kind") is an accommodation on qualifications alone. Do not lower the score for it.',
  '',
  'UNCERTAINTY',
  '- Report what you could not judge in unknowns, as short phrases. Score it as uncertainty: a fact you cannot see moves the score toward the middle of what it could be, never to its best or its worst case. Do not guess it away.',
  '- The "missing" labels already list the gaps code found; do not repeat them in unknowns.',
  '',
  'REASONS',
  '- Each reason is a short phrase or a single word, at most 80 characters ("stairs", "no pets, has a cat", "sent 3 wks ago, no reply"), with the source it came from: voucher_size, authority, rent, area, pets, evictions, accessibility, requirements, preferences, notes, staff_notes, feedback, history, recency, property_details or other.',
  '- Never give a protected characteristic, a credit fact or an income fact as a reason.',
].join('\n');
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D4: about ten SYNTHETIC worked examples spread across the
// bands, including a capped pair, an accommodation pair (assistance animal
// against No pets), an unlawful-requirement pair, a maybe pair and a pair
// with missing inputs. Made-up people and addresses only. Each output must
// survive the production parser untouched (so the examples teach exactly
// the shape the parser keeps) and agree with the production cap and bands.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { TENANT_MATCHING_INPUTS } from '../src/lib/tenantMatchingInputs.js';
import { bandOf } from '../src/services/ranking/bands.js';
import { capOf, flagFieldsOfKind } from '../src/services/ranking/cap.js';
import { EXAMPLES_VERSION, RANKING_EXAMPLES, type RankingExample } from '../src/services/ranking/examples.js';
import { parseRankingText } from '../src/services/ranking/parse.js';
import { buildStartingEntries } from '../src/lib/orgStartingList.js';
import type { ContactItem } from '../src/repos/contactsRepo.js';
import type { UnitItem } from '../src/repos/unitsRepo.js';
import {
  PROPERTY_CARD_FIELDS,
  PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS,
  RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS,

  type CardFieldUse,

import { LANDLORD_DEFAULTS_KEY, LAST_HEARD_FROM_KEY, PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY, type PropertyCardCtx } from '../src/services/ranking/cards.js';

type Card = Record<string, unknown>;

function propertyCardOf(example: RankingExample, handle: string): Card {
  if (example.direction === 'tenants_for_property') return example.anchor.card;
  return example.candidates.find((c) => c.handle === handle)!.card;
}

function tenantCardOf(example: RankingExample, handle: string): Card {
  if (example.direction === 'properties_for_tenant') return example.anchor.card;
  return example.candidates.find((c) => c.handle === handle)!.card;
}

function freeText(card: Card): Record<string, string> {
  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const field of PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS) {
    const value = card[field];
    if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0) out[field] = value.trim();
  }
  return out;
}

function recordedKeys(card: Card): string[] {
  return RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS.filter((key) => {
    const value = card[key];
    return value === true || typeof value === 'number' || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0);
  });
}

function everyKey(value: unknown, out: string[] = []): string[] {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) value.forEach((v) => everyKey(v, out));
  else if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') {
    for (const [key, child] of Object.entries(value as Record<string, unknown>)) {
      out.push(key);
      everyKey(child, out);
    }
  }

}

  example.output.candidates.map((out) => ({ example, out, property: propertyCardOf(example, out.candidateId), tenant: tenantCardOf(example, out.candidateId) })),
);

function capped(p: (typeof pairs)[number]): boolean {
  return capOf({
    failedRequirements: p.out.failedRequirements,
    accommodationFields: flagFieldsOfKind(p.out.fairHousingFlags, 'accommodation'),
    recordedRequirementKeys: recordedKeys(p.property),
    openUnlawfulFields: flagFieldsOfKind(p.out.fairHousingFlags, 'unlawful'),
  }).capped;
}

describe('the worked examples (e1)', () => {
  it('is version e1 with ten examples', () => {
    expect(EXAMPLES_VERSION).toBe('e1');
    expect(RANKING_EXAMPLES).toHaveLength(10);
  });

  it('covers every band and both directions', () => {
    expect(new Set(pairs.map((p) => bandOf(p.out.score)))).toEqual(new Set(['strong', 'good', 'possible', 'weak']));
    expect(new Set(RANKING_EXAMPLES.map((e) => e.direction))).toEqual(new Set(['tenants_for_property', 'properties_for_tenant']));
  });

  it('every output survives the production parser untouched', () => {
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      const handles = example.candidates.map((c) => c.handle);
      const result = parseRankingText(JSON.stringify(example.output), {
        handles,
        freeTextByHandle: new Map(handles.map((h) => [h, freeText(propertyCardOf(example, h))])),
        landlordCard: false,
      });
      expect(result.ok, example.title).toBe(true);
      if (!result.ok) continue;
      expect(result.value.droppedUnlawfulFlags, example.title).toBe(0);
      expect(result.value.byHandle.size, example.title).toBe(example.candidates.length);
      for (const out of example.output.candidates) {
        const { candidateId: _id, ...rest } = out;
        expect(result.value.byHandle.get(out.candidateId), example.title).toEqual(rest);
      }
    }
  });

  it('candidate handles are c1..cn and home handles h1..hn, in order', () => {
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      expect(example.candidates.map((c) => c.handle)).toEqual(example.candidates.map((_c, i) => `c${i + 1}`));
      expect(example.homesSeen.map((h) => h.handle)).toEqual(example.homesSeen.map((_h, i) => `h${i + 1}`));
    }
  });

  it('a capped pair sits in Weak; there are at least two (one a qualifications clause with credit and income in it)', () => {
    const cappedPairs = pairs.filter(capped);
    expect(cappedPairs.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    for (const p of cappedPairs) expect(bandOf(p.out.score), p.example.title).toBe('weak');
    expect(cappedPairs.some((p) => p.out.failedRequirements.includes('no_pets'))).toBe(true);
    expect(cappedPairs.some((p) => p.out.failedRequirements.includes('qualifications') && /credit/i.test(String(p.property['qualifications'])))).toBe(true);
  });

  it('has an accommodation pair: assistance animal against No pets, not capped', () => {
    const p = pairs.find((x) => x.out.fairHousingFlags.some((f) => f.kind === 'accommodation' && f.field === 'no_pets'));
    expect(p).toBeDefined();
    expect(p!.property['no_pets']).toBe(true);
    expect(String(p!.tenant['pets'])).toMatch(/assistance animal/i);
    expect(capped(p!)).toBe(false);
    expect(p!.out.failedRequirements).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('has an unlawful pair: a no-kids rule flagged on a free-text field, noted in unknowns, not capped, not failed', () => {
    const p = pairs.find((x) => x.out.fairHousingFlags.some((f) => f.kind === 'unlawful'));
    expect(p).toBeDefined();
    const flag = p!.out.fairHousingFlags.find((f) => f.kind === 'unlawful')!;
    expect(PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS).toContain(flag.field);
    expect(String(p!.property[flag.field])).toMatch(/no kids/i);
    expect(p!.out.unknowns.some((u) => u.startsWith(`${flag.field}:`))).toBe(true);
    expect(p!.out.failedRequirements).not.toContain(flag.field);
    expect(capped(p!)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('has a maybe pair: a staff decline plus unsure feedback, scored above Weak', () => {
    const p = pairs.find((x) => {
      const history = x.example.candidates.find((c) => c.handle === x.out.candidateId)!.pairHistory;
      return history.declined !== null;
    });
    expect(p).toBeDefined();
    const seen = p!.tenant['propertiesSeen'] as Array<{ feedback: string[] }>;
    expect(seen.some((s) => s.feedback.some((line) => /on the fence/i.test(line)))).toBe(true);
    expect(bandOf(p!.out.score)).not.toBe('weak');
  });

  it('has a pair with missing inputs on both cards', () => {
    expect(RANKING_EXAMPLES.some((e) => e.anchor.missing.length > 0 && e.candidates.some((c) => c.missing.length > 0))).toBe(true);
  });

  it('has a Weak pair that is NOT capped (an accessibility need the home cannot meet)', () => {
    expect(pairs.some((p) => bandOf(p.out.score) === 'weak' && !capped(p) && p.out.against.some((r) => r.source === 'accessibility'))).toBe(true);
  });

  it('every home a propertiesSeen entry names is in homesSeen, is a candidate, or is the property anchor (PR20)', () => {
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      const handles = new Set([...example.homesSeen.map((h) => h.handle), ...example.candidates.map((c) => c.handle)]);
      if (example.direction === 'tenants_for_property') handles.add('anchor');
      const cards = [example.anchor.card, ...example.candidates.map((c) => c.card)];
      for (const card of cards) {
        const seen = card['propertiesSeen'];
        if (!Array.isArray(seen)) continue;
        for (const entry of seen as Array<{ home: string }>) expect(handles.has(entry.home), example.title).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });

  // PR31 / R2F13: the examples are the production wire shape. Each card's
  // `missing` is what S3's OWN completeness functions (propertyMissing /
  // tenantMissing) return for the stored record the card was built from;
  // each card key is one the card builders can emit; each seen entry has
  // the keys S3's tenant card writes; and the three home references (h, c,
  // anchor) all appear.
  const DERIVED_PROPERTY_KEYS = ['voucherSizes', 'voucherSizesInferredFromBeds', 'authorities', LANDLORD_DEFAULTS_KEY];
  const DERIVED_TENANT_KEYS = [LAST_HEARD_FROM_KEY, PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY];
  const ORG_ENTRIES = buildStartingEntries('2026-10-28T00:00:00.000Z', (() => { let n = 0; return () => `ex-org-${(n += 1)}`; })());
  const CTX: PropertyCardCtx = { orgEntries: ORG_ENTRIES, landlordCard: false, landlord: null };

  /** The stored unit an example property card stands for (the card's own keys, derived fields undone). */
  function unitOf(card: Card): UnitItem {
    const record: Record<string, unknown> = { unitId: 'ex-unit', landlordId: 'ex-landlord' };
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(card)) if (!DERIVED_PROPERTY_KEYS.includes(key)) record[key] = value;
    if (card['voucherSizesInferredFromBeds'] !== true) record['voucher_size_accepted'] = card['voucherSizes'];
    const authorities = card['authorities'] as { mapped: string[]; unmapped: string[] };
    record['accepted_authorities'] = [...authorities.mapped, ...authorities.unmapped];
    return record as UnitItem;
  }

  /** The stored contact an example tenant card stands for (list labels mapped back to their keys). */
  function contactOf(card: Card): ContactItem {
    const record: Record<string, unknown> = { contactId: 'ex-contact', type: 'tenant' };
    const keyOfLabel = new Map<string, string>(TENANT_MATCHING_INPUTS.map((e) => [e.label, e.key]));
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(card)) {
      if (DERIVED_TENANT_KEYS.includes(key)) continue;
      record[keyOfLabel.get(key) ?? key] = value;
    }
    return record as ContactItem;
  }

  const labels = (flags: readonly { label: string }[]): string[] => flags.map((f) => f.label);
  const propertyFlags = (card: Card): string[] => labels(propertyMissing(unitOf(card), CTX));
  const tenantFlags = (card: Card): string[] => labels(tenantMissing(contactOf(card)));

  const emittedKeys = (registry: Readonly<Record<string, CardFieldUse>>): Set<string> =>
    new Set(includedFields(registry).map(([key, field]) => field.cardKey ?? key));

  it('every example card key is one the production card builders can emit (R2F13)', () => {
    const propertyKeys = new Set([...emittedKeys(PROPERTY_CARD_FIELDS), ...DERIVED_PROPERTY_KEYS]);
    const tenantKeys = new Set([...emittedKeys(TENANT_CARD_FIELDS), ...DERIVED_TENANT_KEYS]);
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      const anchorIsProperty = example.direction === 'tenants_for_property';
      const check = (card: Card, allowed: Set<string>, who: string): void => {
        for (const key of Object.keys(card)) expect(allowed.has(key), `${example.title}: ${who} key ${key}`).toBe(true);
      };
      check(example.anchor.card, anchorIsProperty ? propertyKeys : tenantKeys, 'anchor');
      for (const c of example.candidates) check(c.card, anchorIsProperty ? tenantKeys : propertyKeys, c.handle);
      for (const h of example.homesSeen) check(h.card, propertyKeys, h.handle);
    }
  });

  it('every missing list is what S3\'s propertyMissing / tenantMissing return for that card\'s record (PR31, R2F13)', () => {
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      const anchorIsProperty = example.direction === 'tenants_for_property';
      expect(example.anchor.missing, `${example.title}: anchor`).toEqual(
        anchorIsProperty ? propertyFlags(example.anchor.card) : tenantFlags(example.anchor.card),
      );
      for (const c of example.candidates) {
        expect(c.missing, `${example.title}: ${c.handle}`).toEqual(anchorIsProperty ? tenantFlags(c.card) : propertyFlags(c.card));
      }
    }
  });

  it('every seen entry has the keys S3 writes, in order, and the label of its home (PR31)', () => {
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      const tenantCards = example.direction === 'tenants_for_property' ? example.candidates.map((c) => c.card) : [example.anchor.card];
      for (const card of tenantCards) {
        for (const entry of (card['propertiesSeen'] as Array<Record<string, unknown>>) ?? []) {
          expect(Object.keys(entry), example.title).toEqual(['home', 'label', 'sends', 'daysSinceLastSend', 'declined', 'tours', 'feedback']);
          const seenHome = example.homesSeen.find((h) => h.handle === entry['home']);
          if (seenHome !== undefined) expect(entry['label']).toBe(seenHome.label);
        }
      }
    }
  });

  it('the examples use all three home references: an h handle, a c handle and the anchor (PR20, PR31)', () => {
    const refs = RANKING_EXAMPLES.flatMap((example) =>
      [example.anchor.card, ...example.candidates.map((c) => c.card)].flatMap((card) =>
        ((card['propertiesSeen'] as Array<{ home: string }>) ?? []).map((entry) => entry.home)),
    );
    expect(refs.some((r) => /^h\d+$/.test(r))).toBe(true);
    expect(refs.some((r) => /^c\d+$/.test(r))).toBe(true);
    expect(refs).toContain('anchor');
  });

  it('is synthetic: no ids, phones or emails on any card; every surname and street is a placeholder word', () => {
    const banned = ['contactId', 'unitId', 'landlordId', 'propertyId', 'phone', 'phones', 'email', 'emails'];
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      for (const key of everyKey(example)) expect(banned, example.title).not.toContain(key);
      const cards = [example.anchor.card, ...example.candidates.map((c) => c.card), ...example.homesSeen.map((h) => h.card)];
      for (const card of cards) {
        if (typeof card['lastName'] === 'string') expect(['Example', 'Sample', 'Placeholder']).toContain(card['lastName']);
        const address = card['address'] as { line1?: string } | undefined;
        if (address?.line1 !== undefined) expect(address.line1).toMatch(/Example|Sample|Placeholder/);
      }
    }
  });

  it('keys the tenant matching inputs by their list labels only', () => {
    const labels = new Set<string>(TENANT_MATCHING_INPUTS.map((e) => e.label));
    for (const example of RANKING_EXAMPLES) {
      for (const key of everyKey(example)) {
        if (/^[A-Z]/.test(key)) expect(labels.has(key), `${example.title}: ${key}`).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });

  it('is ASCII only', () => {
    expect(JSON.stringify(RANKING_EXAMPLES)).toMatch(/^[\x20-\x7e]*$/);
  });
});
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D4 (charter 7.2, 12): the worked examples, version e1. Ten
// SYNTHETIC pairs spread across the bands - made-up people (surnames
// Example, Sample, Placeholder) and made-up streets in real metro-Atlanta
// cities. Each is written in the exact wire shape of a real call (prompt.ts
// renders it with the same renderer as the real user content), followed by
// the output a good answer gives. Cameron checks them at the handback; B2b's
// promotion grows the set and bumps EXAMPLES_VERSION; B2a only reads it.
// ANY edit here is a new EXAMPLES_VERSION (every match records it).
//
// Exempt from the tenant-matching-inputs reader scan (spec D2.1): the cards
// are synthetic and key the inputs by their list LABELS, as real cards do.
import type { RankingSource } from './schema.js';
import type { Card, Direction, PairHistory } from './types.js';

export const EXAMPLES_VERSION = 'e1';

export interface ExampleHome {
  handle: string;
  label: string;
  card: Card;
}

export interface ExampleCandidate {
  handle: string;
  card: Card;
  missing: string[];
  pairHistory: PairHistory;
}

export interface ExampleOutputEntry {
  candidateId: string;
  score: number;
  for: Array<{ text: string; source: RankingSource }>;
  against: Array<{ text: string; source: RankingSource }>;
  unknowns: string[];
  failedRequirements: string[];
  fairHousingFlags: Array<{ kind: 'unlawful' | 'accommodation'; field: string }>;
}

export interface RankingExample {
  title: string;
  direction: Direction;
  anchor: { card: Card; missing: string[] };
  homesSeen: ExampleHome[];
  candidates: ExampleCandidate[];
  output: { candidates: ExampleOutputEntry[] };
}
```

```ts
// Shared ranking-batch fixtures (WP1 B2a): small synthetic cards and the
// buildRankingBatch sources the S4-S8 tests build on. Cards here are plain
// records shaped like S3's cards; propertyFacts is derived the way S3's
// propertyFacts reads a card (free text by field, recorded requirement keys).
import { PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS, RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS } from '../../src/services/ranking/cardFields.js';
import type { PropertyFactsLike, RankingBatchSource } from '../../src/services/ranking/prompt.js';
import type { Card, MissingFlag, PairHistory } from '../../src/services/ranking/types.js';

export const NO_HISTORY: PairHistory = { sends: [], declined: null, tours: [], daysSinceLastSend: null };

export function propertyCardFixture(over: Card = {}): Card {
  return {
    address: { line1: '10 Fixture Street', city: 'Decatur', state: 'GA', zip: '30030' },
    beds: 2,
    baths: 1,
    area: 'Decatur',
    rent_min: 1400,
    payment_standard: 1600,
    notes: 'Fenced yard',
    status: 'available',
    voucherSizes: [2],
    voucherSizesInferredFromBeds: false,
    authorities: { mapped: ['Decatur Housing Authority'], unmapped: [] },
    ...over,
  };
}

export function tenantCardFixture(over: Card = {}): Card {
  return {
    firstName: 'Fixture',
    lastName: 'Tenant',
    voucherSize: 2,
    housingAuthority: 'Decatur Housing Authority',
    status: 'searching',
    notes: 'Works days.',
    lastHeardFrom: 'this week',
    propertiesSeen: [],
    ...over,
  };
}

export function factsOf(card: Card): PropertyFactsLike {
  const recordedRequirementKeys = RANKED_REQUIREMENT_KEYS.filter((key) => {
    const value = card[key];
    return value === true || typeof value === 'number' || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0);
  });
  const freeTextByField: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const field of PROPERTY_FREE_TEXT_FIELDS) {
    const value = card[field];
    if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0) freeTextByField[field] = value.trim();
  }
  return { recordedRequirementKeys, freeTextByField };
}

export function missing(...labels: string[]): MissingFlag[] {
  return labels.map((label, i) => ({ key: `missing_${i + 1}`, label }));
}

export interface FixtureOptions {
  homes?: Map<string, { label: string; card: Card }>;
  landlordCard?: boolean;
  batchIndex?: number;
}

/** A property anchor ('unit-anchor') with these tenant cards as candidates tenant-1..n. */
export function tenantsForPropertySource(tenants: Card[], property: Card = propertyCardFixture(), opts: FixtureOptions = {}): RankingBatchSource {
  return {
    direction: 'tenants_for_property',
    batchIndex: opts.batchIndex ?? 0,
    landlordCard: opts.landlordCard ?? false,
    anchor: { card: property, missing: [] },
    candidates: tenants.map((card, i) => ({
      candidateId: `tenant-${i + 1}`,
      unitId: 'unit-anchor',
      card,
      missing: [],
      pairHistory: NO_HISTORY,
      propertyFacts: factsOf(property),
    })),
    homes: opts.homes ?? new Map(),
  };
}

/** A tenant anchor with these properties as candidates (candidateId = unitId). */
export function propertiesForTenantSource(
  properties: Array<{ unitId: string; card: Card }>,
  tenant: Card = tenantCardFixture(),
  opts: FixtureOptions = {},
): RankingBatchSource {
  return {
    direction: 'properties_for_tenant',
    batchIndex: opts.batchIndex ?? 0,
    landlordCard: opts.landlordCard ?? false,
    anchor: { card: tenant, missing: [] },
    candidates: properties.map((p) => ({
      candidateId: p.unitId,
      unitId: p.unitId,
      card: p.card,
      missing: [],
      pairHistory: NO_HISTORY,
      propertyFacts: factsOf(p.card),
    })),
    homes: opts.homes ?? new Map(),
  };
}
```

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D4 "The call" and D8.1: the system text (rubric then the
// worked examples, byte-stable), the user content (anchor, homesSeen written
// once each, candidates by handle in pool order), promptFingerprint (sha256
// of the system text) and the per-pair input snapshot.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { RANKING_EXAMPLES } from '../src/services/ranking/examples.js';
import {
  PROMPT_FRAMING,
  RankingPromptError,
  buildRankingBatch,
  buildRankingPrompt,
  buildRankingSystemPrompt,
  rankingPromptFingerprint,
  renderExamplesText,
  renderUserContent,
  snapshotOf,
  stableJson,
} from '../src/services/ranking/prompt.js';
import { RUBRIC_TEXT } from '../src/services/ranking/rubric.js';
import { rankingSchema } from '../src/services/ranking/schema.js';
import {
  factsOf,
  missing,
  propertiesForTenantSource,
  propertyCardFixture,
  tenantCardFixture,
  tenantsForPropertySource,
} from './helpers/rankingBatchFixture.js';

function inputJson(user: string): Record<string, unknown> {
  const lines = user.split('\n');
  expect(lines[2]).toBe('INPUT:');
  return JSON.parse(lines.slice(3).join('\n')) as Record<string, unknown>;
}

const seenEntry = (home: string) => ({
  home,
  sends: [{ at: '2026-10-01', kind: 'sent' }],
  daysSinceLastSend: 20,
  declined: null,
  tours: [],
  feedback: [],
});

describe('the system text', () => {
  it('is the rubric, then the worked examples, every example once in order', () => {
    const system = buildRankingSystemPrompt();
    expect(system.startsWith(`${RUBRIC_TEXT}\n\nWORKED EXAMPLES`)).toBe(true);
    let at = 0;
    RANKING_EXAMPLES.forEach((example, i) => {
      const heading = `EXAMPLE ${i + 1}: ${example.title}`;
      const found = system.indexOf(heading, at);
      expect(found, heading).toBeGreaterThan(at);
      at = found;
    });
  });

  it('renders each example with the real user-content renderer, then its output', () => {
    const system = buildRankingSystemPrompt();
    const first = RANKING_EXAMPLES[0]!;
    const rendered = renderUserContent(first.direction, { anchor: first.anchor, homesSeen: first.homesSeen, candidates: first.candidates });
    expect(system).toContain(`EXAMPLE 1: ${first.title}\n${rendered}\nOUTPUT:\n${JSON.stringify(first.output)}`);
  });

  it('R2F3: every framing string lives in the frozen PROMPT_FRAMING, and the system text ends with the rendered examples', () => {
    expect(Object.isFrozen(PROMPT_FRAMING)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(PROMPT_FRAMING.directionLines)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.keys(PROMPT_FRAMING.directionLines).sort()).toEqual(['properties_for_tenant', 'tenants_for_property']);
    const first = RANKING_EXAMPLES[0]!;
    const rendered = renderUserContent(first.direction, { anchor: first.anchor, homesSeen: first.homesSeen, candidates: first.candidates });
    expect(rendered.split('\n').slice(0, 3)).toEqual([
      PROMPT_FRAMING.directionLines[first.direction],
      PROMPT_FRAMING.instructionLine,
      PROMPT_FRAMING.inputLine,
    ]);
    expect(buildRankingSystemPrompt()).toBe(`${RUBRIC_TEXT}\n\n${PROMPT_FRAMING.examplesHeading}\n\n${renderExamplesText()}`);
    expect(renderExamplesText().startsWith(`${PROMPT_FRAMING.examplePrefix} 1: ${first.title}\n`)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('is byte-stable and ASCII only', () => {
    expect(buildRankingSystemPrompt()).toBe(buildRankingSystemPrompt());
    expect(buildRankingSystemPrompt()).toMatch(/^[\t\n\x20-\x7e]*$/);
  });

  it('promptFingerprint (PR18) is sha256 over the system text, a newline and the stable JSON of the schema sent', () => {
    for (const landlordCard of [false, true]) {
      const expected = createHash('sha256')
        .update(`${buildRankingSystemPrompt()}\n${stableJson(rankingSchema({ landlordCard }))}`, 'utf8')
        .digest('hex');
      expect(rankingPromptFingerprint({ landlordCard })).toBe(expected);
      expect(rankingPromptFingerprint({ landlordCard })).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
    }
    expect(rankingPromptFingerprint({ landlordCard: true })).not.toBe(rankingPromptFingerprint({ landlordCard: false }));
  });

  it('stableJson sorts object keys at every depth and keeps array order', () => {
    expect(stableJson({ b: 1, a: { d: [2, 1], c: 'x' } })).toBe('{"a":{"c":"x","d":[2,1]},"b":1}');
    expect(stableJson({ a: 1, b: undefined })).toBe('{"a":1}');
  });
});

describe('buildRankingBatch - handles and the user content', () => {
  it('hands out c1..cn in pool order and never puts a record id in the text', () => {
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource([
      tenantCardFixture({ firstName: 'Ann' }),
      tenantCardFixture({ firstName: 'Ben' }),
      tenantCardFixture({ firstName: 'Cy' }),
    ]));
    expect(batch.handles).toEqual([
      { handle: 'c1', candidateId: 'tenant-1', unitId: 'unit-anchor' },

      { handle: 'c3', candidateId: 'tenant-3', unitId: 'unit-anchor' },
    ]);
    expect(batch.wire.candidates.map((c) => [c.handle, c.card['firstName']])).toEqual([['c1', 'Ann'], ['c2', 'Ben'], ['c3', 'Cy']]);
    expect(batch.user).not.toContain('tenant-1');
    expect(batch.user).not.toContain('unit-anchor');
  });

  it('the user content is the direction line, the instruction, INPUT: and the wire as JSON', () => {
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource([tenantCardFixture()]));
    const lines = batch.user.split('\n');
    expect(lines[0]).toBe('DIRECTION: tenants_for_property - the anchor is a property; every candidate is a tenant.');
    expect(lines[1]).toBe('Score every candidate. Return exactly one entry per candidate handle, with the handle as candidateId.');
    expect(inputJson(batch.user)).toEqual(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(batch.wire)));
    expect(Object.keys(batch.wire)).toEqual(['anchor', 'homesSeen', 'candidates']);
    expect(Object.keys(batch.wire.candidates[0]!)).toEqual(['handle', 'card', 'missing', 'pairHistory']);
  });

  it('the tenant anchor direction line', () => {
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(propertiesForTenantSource([{ unitId: 'u-1', card: propertyCardFixture() }]));
    expect(batch.user.split('\n')[0]).toBe('DIRECTION: properties_for_tenant - the anchor is a tenant; every candidate is a property.');
  });

  it('sends missing flags as their labels', () => {
    const src = tenantsForPropertySource([tenantCardFixture()]);
    const batch = buildRankingBatch({
      ...src,

    expect(batch.wire.candidates[0]!.missing).toEqual(['Area preference', 'Maximum tenant portion']);
  });

  it('carries the system text, the fingerprint, the batch index and the landlord switch', () => {
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource([tenantCardFixture()], propertyCardFixture(), { batchIndex: 3, landlordCard: true }));
    expect(batch.system).toBe(buildRankingSystemPrompt());
    expect(batch.promptFingerprint).toBe(rankingPromptFingerprint({ landlordCard: true }));
    expect(batch.batchIndex).toBe(3);
    expect(batch.landlordCard).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('buildRankingBatch - homesSeen', () => {
  const homeA = { label: '1 Seen Street, Decatur', card: propertyCardFixture({ notes: 'home A' }) };
  const homeB = { label: '2 Seen Street, Tucker', card: propertyCardFixture({ notes: 'home B' }) };

  it('writes each distinct home ONCE, h1..hn in first-reference order, and points every entry at it', () => {
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource(
      [
        tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('u-b'), seenEntry('u-a')] }),
        tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('u-a')] }),
      ],
      propertyCardFixture(),
      { homes: new Map([['u-a', homeA], ['u-b', homeB]]) },
    ));
    expect(batch.wire.homesSeen).toEqual([
      { handle: 'h1', label: homeB.label, card: homeB.card },
      { handle: 'h2', label: homeA.label, card: homeA.card },
    ]);
    const seen1 = batch.wire.candidates[0]!.card['propertiesSeen'] as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
    const seen2 = batch.wire.candidates[1]!.card['propertiesSeen'] as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
    expect(seen1.map((e) => e['home'])).toEqual(['h1', 'h2']);
    expect(seen2.map((e) => e['home'])).toEqual(['h2']);
    expect(Object.keys(seen1[0]!)).toEqual(['home', 'sends', 'daysSinceLastSend', 'declined', 'tours', 'feedback']);
    expect(batch.user).not.toContain('u-a');
  });

  it('a seen home that is also a candidate is written once, as the candidate, and referenced by its c handle', () => {
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(propertiesForTenantSource(
      [{ unitId: 'u-1', card: propertyCardFixture({ notes: 'cand 1' }) }, { unitId: 'u-2', card: propertyCardFixture({ notes: 'cand 2' }) }],
      tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('u-2'), seenEntry('u-9')] }),
      { homes: new Map([['u-2', { label: '2 Cand Road, Decatur', card: propertyCardFixture({ notes: 'cand 2' }) }], ['u-9', homeA]]) },
    ));
    const seen = batch.wire.anchor.card['propertiesSeen'] as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
    expect(seen.map((e) => e['home'])).toEqual(['c2', 'h1']);
    expect(batch.wire.homesSeen).toEqual([{ handle: 'h1', label: homeA.label, card: homeA.card }]);
    expect(batch.homeLabelByHandle.get('c2')).toBe('2 Cand Road, Decatur');
    expect(batch.homeLabelByHandle.get('h1')).toBe(homeA.label);
  });

  it('PR20: a seen home that IS the property anchor is home "anchor", never written to homesSeen', () => {
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource(
      [tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('unit-anchor'), seenEntry('u-a')] })],
      propertyCardFixture(),
      { homes: new Map([['unit-anchor', { label: '10 Fixture Street, Decatur', card: propertyCardFixture() }], ['u-a', homeA]]) },
    ));
    const seen = batch.wire.candidates[0]!.card['propertiesSeen'] as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
    expect(seen.map((e) => e['home'])).toEqual(['anchor', 'h1']);
    expect(batch.wire.homesSeen).toEqual([{ handle: 'h1', label: homeA.label, card: homeA.card }]);
    expect(batch.homeLabelByHandle.get('anchor')).toBe('10 Fixture Street, Decatur');
  });

  it('PR20 / IR17: no unitId reaches the user text, whichever of the three references an entry gets', () => {
    const tenantSide = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource(
      [tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('unit-anchor'), seenEntry('u-a')] })],
      propertyCardFixture(),
      { homes: new Map([['unit-anchor', { label: '10 Fixture Street, Decatur', card: propertyCardFixture() }], ['u-a', homeA]]) },
    ));
    for (const id of ['unit-anchor', 'u-a']) expect(tenantSide.user).not.toContain(id);
    const propertySide = buildRankingBatch(propertiesForTenantSource(
      [{ unitId: 'u-1', card: propertyCardFixture() }, { unitId: 'u-2', card: propertyCardFixture() }],
      tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('u-2'), seenEntry('u-9')] }),
      { homes: new Map([['u-2', { label: '2 Cand Road, Decatur', card: propertyCardFixture() }], ['u-9', homeB]]) },
    ));
    for (const id of ['u-1', 'u-2', 'u-9']) expect(propertySide.user).not.toContain(id);
  });

  it('throws RankingPromptError for a home the batch does not carry', () => {
    expect(() => buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource([tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('u-missing')] })])))
      .toThrow(RankingPromptError);
  });

  it('leaves an entry without a string home as it is, and a card without propertiesSeen untouched', () => {
    const odd = { sends: [], feedback: ['x'] };
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource([tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [odd] })]));
    expect(batch.wire.candidates[0]!.card['propertiesSeen']).toEqual([odd]);
    expect(batch.wire.anchor.card).toEqual(propertyCardFixture());
  });

  it('never mutates the cards it was given', () => {
    const card = tenantCardFixture({ propertiesSeen: [seenEntry('u-a')] });
    const before = JSON.stringify(card);
    buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource([card], propertyCardFixture(), { homes: new Map([['u-a', homeA]]) }));
    expect(JSON.stringify(card)).toBe(before);
  });
});

describe('buildRankingBatch - the parse context', () => {
  it('a property anchor: every handle reads the anchor property free text', () => {
    const property = propertyCardFixture({ qualifications: 'No kids.' });
    const batch = buildRankingBatch(tenantsForPropertySource([tenantCardFixture(), tenantCardFixture()], property));
    expect(batch.freeTextByHandle.get('c1')).toEqual(factsOf(property).freeTextByField);
    expect(batch.freeTextByHandle.get('c2')).toEqual(factsOf(property).freeTextByField);
  });

  it('a tenant anchor: each handle reads its own property', () => {

    const b = propertyCardFixture({ notes: 'B' });

    expect(batch.freeTextByHandle.get('c1')!['notes']).toBe('A');
    expect(batch.freeTextByHandle.get('c2')!['notes']).toBe('B');
  });
});

describe('snapshotOf (spec D8.1)', () => {
  it('holds the anchor and the candidate as sent, and every home either tenant card references, resolved', () => {
    const homeA = { label: '1 Seen Street, Decatur', card: propertyCardFixture({ notes: 'home A' }) };
```

#### Step 3 - implementation

Create `app/src/services/ranking/prompt.ts`:

```ts
// WP1 B2a spec D4 "The call" and D8.1: the text of one ranking call.
//
// - system = RUBRIC_TEXT, then the worked examples, byte-stable for a given
//   pair of versions (RUBRIC_VERSION, EXAMPLES_VERSION). Each example is
//   rendered with renderUserContent - the renderer the real user content
//   uses - so the examples look exactly like a real call.
// - user = a direction line, one instruction line, "INPUT:", then one JSON
//   object: { anchor: { card, missing }, homesSeen, candidates }.
//   * candidates carry handles c1..cn in pool order; record ids never reach
//     the text (handles map back through RankingBatchInput.handles).
//   * homesSeen holds every distinct home any tenant card in the call lists
//     under propertiesSeen, written ONCE as { handle, label, card } with
//     handles h1..hn in first-reference order; each propertiesSeen entry's
//     `home` (the unitId S3 puts there) is replaced by its reference
//     (PR20): "anchor" for the property ANCHOR itself (its card is the
//     anchor card, written once), the c handle for a seen home that is a
//     candidate in the same call (a tenant anchor), and the h handle in
//     homesSeen for any other home.
// - promptFingerprint (PR18) = sha256 over the system text, a newline, and
//   the stable JSON of the schema sent on the call (keys sorted), so a
//   schema change - and each landlord-switch state - has its own
//   fingerprint. Recorded on every run.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { RANKING_EXAMPLES, type RankingExample } from './examples.js';
import { RUBRIC_TEXT } from './rubric.js';
import { rankingSchema } from './schema.js';
import type { Card, Direction, MissingFlag, PairHistory } from './types.js';

/** The tenant card key holding the seen homes (spec D2.1) and the entry key naming the home (S3, PR20). */
export const PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY = 'propertiesSeen';
export const SEEN_HOME_KEY = 'home';
/** PR20: how a seen home that IS the property anchor is referenced in the call. */
export const ANCHOR_HOME_HANDLE = 'anchor';

export interface WireHome {
  handle: string;
  label: string;
  card: Card;
}

export interface WireCandidate {
  handle: string;
  card: Card;
  missing: string[];
  pairHistory: PairHistory;
}

export interface RankingWire {
  anchor: { card: Card; missing: string[] };
  homesSeen: WireHome[];
  candidates: WireCandidate[];
}

/** What S3's propertyFacts gives for the pair's property. */
export interface PropertyFactsLike {
  recordedRequirementKeys: readonly string[];
  freeTextByField: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
}

export interface RankingBatchCandidateSource {
  candidateId: string;
  /** The pair's property: the anchor unit for a property anchor, the candidate unit for a tenant anchor. */
  unitId: string;
  card: Card;
  missing: readonly MissingFlag[];
  pairHistory: PairHistory;
  propertyFacts: PropertyFactsLike;
}

export interface RankingBatchSource {
  direction: Direction;
  batchIndex: number;
  landlordCard: boolean;
  anchor: { card: Card; missing: readonly MissingFlag[] };
  candidates: readonly RankingBatchCandidateSource[];
  /** Every home any tenant card in the batch references (S3's assemble), keyed by unitId. */
  homes: ReadonlyMap<string, { label: string; card: Card }>;
}

export interface RankingHandle {
  handle: string;
  candidateId: string;
  unitId: string;
}

export interface RankingBatchInput {
  direction: Direction;
  batchIndex: number;
  landlordCard: boolean;
  system: string;
  user: string;
  promptFingerprint: string;
  wire: RankingWire;
  handles: readonly RankingHandle[];
  /** Per handle: the free text of that pair's property card (the unlawful-flag rule). */
  freeTextByHandle: ReadonlyMap<string, Readonly<Record<string, string>>>;
  /** Per home reference a seen entry uses (h, c or "anchor"): its label. */
  homeLabelByHandle: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
}

/** Spec D8.1: the exact JSON one pair was scored from (S5 gzips it onto the match). */
export interface RankingPairSnapshot {
  direction: Direction;
  anchor: { card: Card; missing: string[] };
  candidate: WireCandidate;
  homes: WireHome[];
}

/** A batch that cannot be written (a seen home the batch does not carry). S5 records it as a failed batch. */
export class RankingPromptError extends Error {}

/**
 * Every framing string of the call, in ONE frozen object (R2F3): the user
 * message's direction and instruction lines and the system text's examples
 * framing. S4.11 pins sha256 of JSON.stringify(PROMPT_FRAMING) beside
 * RUBRIC_VERSION, so an edit to any of them is a version decision.
 */
export const PROMPT_FRAMING = Object.freeze({
  directionLines: Object.freeze({
    tenants_for_property: 'DIRECTION: tenants_for_property - the anchor is a property; every candidate is a tenant.',
    properties_for_tenant: 'DIRECTION: properties_for_tenant - the anchor is a tenant; every candidate is a property.',
  } satisfies Record<Direction, string>),
  instructionLine: 'Score every candidate. Return exactly one entry per candidate handle, with the handle as candidateId.',
  inputLine: 'INPUT:',
  examplesHeading: 'WORKED EXAMPLES (synthetic people and homes; each shows an input and a good output)',
  examplePrefix: 'EXAMPLE',
  outputLine: 'OUTPUT:',
});

export function renderUserContent(direction: Direction, wire: RankingWire): string {
  return [PROMPT_FRAMING.directionLines[direction], PROMPT_FRAMING.instructionLine, PROMPT_FRAMING.inputLine, JSON.stringify(wire)].join('\n');
}

function renderExample(example: RankingExample, n: number): string {
  const wire: RankingWire = { anchor: example.anchor, homesSeen: example.homesSeen, candidates: example.candidates };
  return [
    `${PROMPT_FRAMING.examplePrefix} ${n}: ${example.title}`,
    renderUserContent(example.direction, wire),
    PROMPT_FRAMING.outputLine,
    JSON.stringify(example.output),
  ].join('\n');
}

/** The worked examples exactly as the system text carries them (R2F3: S4.11 pins this beside EXAMPLES_VERSION). */
export function renderExamplesText(): string {
  return RANKING_EXAMPLES.map((example, i) => renderExample(example, i + 1)).join('\n\n');
}

let systemCache: string | undefined;
export function buildRankingSystemPrompt(): string {
  systemCache ??= [RUBRIC_TEXT, '', PROMPT_FRAMING.examplesHeading, '', renderExamplesText()].join('\n');
  return systemCache;
}

/** JSON with every object's keys sorted, so the same value always gives the same bytes (PR18). */
export function stableJson(value: unknown): string {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map((item) => stableJson(item)).join(',')}]`;
  if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') {
    const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
    const keys = Object.keys(record).filter((key) => record[key] !== undefined).sort();
    return `{${keys.map((key) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${stableJson(record[key])}`).join(',')}}`;
  }
  return JSON.stringify(value);
}

const fingerprintCache = new Map<boolean, string>();
/** PR18: sha256 over the system text, a newline, and the stable JSON of the schema this call sends. */
export function rankingPromptFingerprint(opts: { landlordCard: boolean }): string {
  let fingerprint = fingerprintCache.get(opts.landlordCard);
  if (fingerprint === undefined) {
    fingerprint = createHash('sha256')
      .update(buildRankingSystemPrompt(), 'utf8')
      .update('\n', 'utf8')
      .update(stableJson(rankingSchema({ landlordCard: opts.landlordCard })), 'utf8')
      .digest('hex');
    fingerprintCache.set(opts.landlordCard, fingerprint);
  }
  return fingerprint;
}

function isEntry(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);
}

/** A copy of the card with each propertiesSeen entry's `home` replaced by its handle (key order kept). */
function rewriteSeen(card: Card, handleFor: (unitId: string) => string): Card {
  const seen = card[PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY];
  if (!Array.isArray(seen)) return card;
  const entries = (seen as unknown[]).map((entry) => {
    if (!isEntry(entry)) return entry;
    const ref = entry[SEEN_HOME_KEY];
    return typeof ref === 'string' ? { ...entry, [SEEN_HOME_KEY]: handleFor(ref) } : entry;
  });
  return { ...card, [PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY]: entries };
}

export function buildRankingBatch(src: RankingBatchSource): RankingBatchInput {
  const handles: RankingHandle[] = src.candidates.map((c, i) => ({ handle: `c${i + 1}`, candidateId: c.candidateId, unitId: c.unitId }));
  // Only a tenant anchor has property candidates a seen entry can name.
  const candidateHandleByUnit = new Map<string, string>();
  if (src.direction === 'properties_for_tenant') {
    for (const h of handles) candidateHandleByUnit.set(h.unitId, h.handle);
  }
  // PR20: for a property anchor every candidate's unitId IS the anchor unit
  // (the pair's property), so a seen entry naming it is the anchor itself.
  const anchorUnitId = src.direction === 'tenants_for_property' ? src.candidates[0]?.unitId : undefined;
  const homesSeen: WireHome[] = [];
  const homeHandleByUnit = new Map<string, string>();
  const homeLabelByHandle = new Map<string, string>();
  const handleFor = (unitId: string): string => {
    if (anchorUnitId !== undefined && unitId === anchorUnitId) {
      const label = src.homes.get(unitId)?.label;
      if (label !== undefined) homeLabelByHandle.set(ANCHOR_HOME_HANDLE, label);
      return ANCHOR_HOME_HANDLE;
    }
    const asCandidate = candidateHandleByUnit.get(unitId);
    if (asCandidate !== undefined) {
      const label = src.homes.get(unitId)?.label;
      if (label !== undefined) homeLabelByHandle.set(asCandidate, label);
      return asCandidate;
    }
    const known = homeHandleByUnit.get(unitId);
    if (known !== undefined) return known;
    const home = src.homes.get(unitId);
    if (home === undefined) {
      throw new RankingPromptError('ranking prompt: a properties-seen entry names a home the batch does not carry');
    }
    const handle = `h${homesSeen.length + 1}`;
    homeHandleByUnit.set(unitId, handle);
    homeLabelByHandle.set(handle, home.label);
    homesSeen.push({ handle, label: home.label, card: home.card });
    return handle;
  };
  const anchorCard = rewriteSeen(src.anchor.card, handleFor);
  const candidates: WireCandidate[] = src.candidates.map((c, i) => ({
    handle: handles[i]!.handle,
    card: rewriteSeen(c.card, handleFor),
    missing: c.missing.map((flag) => flag.label),
    pairHistory: c.pairHistory,
  }));
  const wire: RankingWire = {
    anchor: { card: anchorCard, missing: src.anchor.missing.map((flag) => flag.label) },
    homesSeen,
    candidates,
  };
  const freeTextByHandle = new Map<string, Readonly<Record<string, string>>>(
    src.candidates.map((c, i) => [handles[i]!.handle, c.propertyFacts.freeTextByField] as const),
  );
  return {
    direction: src.direction,
    batchIndex: src.batchIndex,
    landlordCard: src.landlordCard,
    system: buildRankingSystemPrompt(),
    user: renderUserContent(src.direction, wire),
    promptFingerprint: rankingPromptFingerprint({ landlordCard: src.landlordCard }),
    wire,
    handles,
    freeTextByHandle,
    homeLabelByHandle,
  };
}

function homeRefs(card: Card): string[] {
  const seen = card[PROPERTIES_SEEN_KEY];
  if (!Array.isArray(seen)) return [];
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const entry of seen as unknown[]) {
    if (!isEntry(entry)) continue;
    const ref = entry[SEEN_HOME_KEY];
    if (typeof ref === 'string' && !out.includes(ref)) out.push(ref);
  }
  return out;
}

export function snapshotOf(batch: RankingBatchInput, handle: string): RankingPairSnapshot | undefined {
  const candidate = batch.wire.candidates.find((c) => c.handle === handle);
  if (candidate === undefined) return undefined;
  const refs: string[] = [];
  for (const ref of [...homeRefs(batch.wire.anchor.card), ...homeRefs(candidate.card)]) {
    if (!refs.includes(ref)) refs.push(ref);
  }
  const homes: WireHome[] = [];
  for (const ref of refs) {
    if (ref === ANCHOR_HOME_HANDLE) {
      homes.push({ handle: ref, label: batch.homeLabelByHandle.get(ref) ?? '', card: batch.wire.anchor.card });
      continue;
    }
    const seen = batch.wire.homesSeen.find((h) => h.handle === ref);
    if (seen !== undefined) {
      homes.push(seen);
      continue;
    }
    const asCandidate = batch.wire.candidates.find((c) => c.handle === ref);
    if (asCandidate !== undefined) {
      homes.push({ handle: ref, label: batch.homeLabelByHandle.get(ref) ?? '', card: asCandidate.card });
    }
  }
  return { direction: batch.direction, anchor: batch.wire.anchor, candidate, homes };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The job-facing wrapper (plan C12): the names S5 codes against.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface RankingPromptHandle {
  handle: string;
  candidateId: string;
  display: string;
}

export interface RankingPrompt {
  /** What driver.rankBatch takes. */
  batchInput: RankingBatchInput;
  /** The user message as sent (S5 gzips it onto the run, spec D11). */
  userText: string;
  promptFingerprint: string;
  /** c1..cn in batch (= pool) order, with the display each candidate was sent under. */
  handles: RankingPromptHandle[];
  /** Spec D8.1 for one candidate; throws RankingPromptError for an id not in the batch. */
  snapshotOf(candidateId: string): RankingPairSnapshot;
}

export interface RankingPromptInput {
  direction: Direction;
  batchIndex: number;
  landlordCard: boolean;
  anchor: { card: Card; missing: readonly MissingFlag[] };
  candidates: ReadonlyArray<RankingBatchCandidateSource & { display: string }>;
  homes: ReadonlyMap<string, { label: string; card: Card }>;
}

export function buildRankingPrompt(input: RankingPromptInput): RankingPrompt {
  const batchInput = buildRankingBatch(input);
  const handles: RankingPromptHandle[] = batchInput.handles.map((h, i) => ({
    handle: h.handle,
    candidateId: h.candidateId,
    display: input.candidates[i]!.display,
  }));
  return {
    batchInput,
    userText: batchInput.user,
    promptFingerprint: batchInput.promptFingerprint,
    handles,
    snapshotOf(candidateId: string): RankingPairSnapshot {
      const handle = handles.find((h) => h.candidateId === candidateId)?.handle;
      const snapshot = handle === undefined ? undefined : snapshotOf(batchInput, handle);
      if (snapshot === undefined) throw new RankingPromptError('ranking prompt: no candidate with that id in this batch');
      return snapshot;
    },
  };
}
```
